in writing. in a period of economic recession and the resulting lack of budgetary resources, but also of increasingly fierce global competition, it is vital for the european union to improve its innovation capacity in a sustainable way. the past has shown that, often, without a comprehensive overall strategy, eu investments in general, including those in research, development and innovation (rdi), do not deliver the desired results: the range of beneficiaries was too wide, the decisions of the political world were too far removed from the real situation on the ground, and the connections between the actors involved and the levels of the administration were insufficient. in the face of the delicate budgetary and economic situation, broad support for many sectors, often unrelated to each other, according to the 'springboard' principle, is no longer feasible. it is now particularly important to be careful when choosing the objectives to be supported. successful collaboration between all actors at all levels will be crucial in this respect.

in writing. - i fully support the report by mr prodi which makes a number of proposals to tackle the problem of plastic waste in our environment. global plastic production has increased dramatically in recent decades. production has increased from 1.5 million tonnes in 1950 to 245 million tonnes in 2008, of which 60 million tonnes in europe. plastic waste often contains dangerous pollutants. it can persist in the environment for hundreds of years and have a negative impact on our ecosystem and our food chain. of the 25 million pieces of plastic waste produced in 2008, 50% was buried, 30% incinerated and 20% recycled. so there's still work to be done. i am therefore pleased that the report sets binding targets for the collection, sorting and recycling of plastic waste, and that it looks at the elimination of hazardous substances from both recycled plastics and new products. in addition, waste incineration is being discouraged, the packaging directive will be reviewed and work is being done to radically reduce and phase out single-use bags. this approach deserves our support.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all recall some useful points to help us appreciate the importance of these interlinked issues. first, public procurement accounts for almost 20% of the eu's gdp and must therefore be used as a lever to foster sustainable and inclusive growth. in december 2011, commissioner barnier, and thus the commission, published two communications on the modernisation of public procurement, for both conventional and special sectors, in order to make procedures more efficient, simple, transparent and accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises. almost 2 500 amendments were tabled to the two directives for which i was and still am the rapporteur. eight parliamentary committees have issued an opinion and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has been working on the substance for a year and a half of negotiations, first within parliament and then in trilogue with the council and the commission. i may perhaps emphasize eight points which i think are essential. there's probably more. the first point concerns the strengthening and clarification of public-public cooperation under article 11. the negotiations on public-public cooperation were very successful, as for the first time the legislator codifies this cooperation by allowing a clear line to be drawn which excludes from the scope of the directive contracts between public authorities and entities with a limited share of private capital. new provisions in article 1 lay down the principle of free administration at all levels of government. it is up to them to decide whether, how and to what extent public interest tasks will be carried out but also in cooperation with other public authorities. the second point concerns general principles. the reference will now be to compliance with national directives and laws, of course, but also with collective agreements. this principle is articulated throughout the directive in such a way as to give a coherent structure guaranteeing respect for labour law and collective agreements in the place where work is carried out. finally, the commission put an end to the many abuses which had led to social and environmental dumping practices, thereby distorting the functioning of the internal market. the third point is a very important provision on subcontracting to prevent it from being used as a means of circumventing the rules on compliance with social and environmental criteria. the new rules on subcontracting impose an obligation on the economic operator to provide all information concerning the part of the contract which he subcontracts and information on subcontractors. in addition, this new article defines the principle of joint responsibility in the subcontracting chain, which member states may establish and strengthen. it should be noted that subcontracting is desirable because it provides an opportunity for small and medium-sized enterprises to participate in public procurement procedures. it just needs to be done under the right conditions. the fourth point concerns the most economically advantageous offer, which is a clear signal. this will now be the only award criterion, which will encourage the authorities to choose the quality and sustainability of public procurement and investment in the light of social, environmental and sustainability criteria, with price obviously remaining one of the criteria. the fifth point is abnormally low tenders, which will now have to be monitored by the authority and rejected if they contravene the general principles of respect for collective agreements and the rules on subcontracting and respect for the environment. the sixth point is the simplification which will be achieved, in particular by encouraging the use of the electronic procedure and self-certification (european single procurement document), which will no longer oblige companies to submit a priori annexes, often cumbersome, which will now be required of the successful tenderer. this is a crucial simplification. the seventh point concerns better access for small and mediumsized enterprises through a reduction in the turnover required to participate in a market and the provision to encourage the temporary grouping of small enterprises to better deal with the issue of public procurement. finally, social services are the subject of a specific title which aims to give them special importance. the directive ensures, in addition to the principles of high quality and inclusion, a balance between a streamlined procedure and the transparency of the award. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this reform is a crucial step towards harmonizing the internal market. our efforts are now moving in the right direction, towards the much-needed economic recovery, sustainable and innovative growth, respect for social rights and our environment. the task is not finished and it will be up to the member states to transpose the directives into national law. i hope they do so by remaining as faithful as possible to the principles that inspired them. i would like to conclude by saying that i do not forget the usual thanks, but i intend to use the two minutes i will be given at the end of the debate to thank the main actors in this directive.

i am sorry to have to say that i have not been able to make a reply to the question. president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i do not agree with the rapporteur, mrs girling, and i do not agree with mr borg. my group rather shares the analysis of mr peterle and mr tabajdi. the committee on the environment and food safety rightly agrees with the court of justice ruling that pollen, and certainly gmo pollen, is an ingredient. pollen is introduced into honey by bees and by the beekeeper's rocking of the honey, but also by human intervention. since hives are deliberately placed somewhere, whether or not near gmo fields, so that the bees can collect pollen from specific plants, and since the honey-sweeping is also deliberate, the presence of pollen in honey cannot be considered unforeseen. common pollen can still be considered a natural ingredient, gmo pollen by definition cannot, because the gmo legislation is based on the fact that gmos are not natural and therefore require risk analysis, authorisation and labelling. so if we consider pollen as an ingredient, then gmo labelling is sufficient for us, there is no need for an ingredient list, as mr tabajdi also said. some argue that the court of justice ruling implies an obligation that all honey will now have to be tested for the presence of gmos as a standard. that's not true. and that will not cost any extra money either, because in practice, ladies and gentlemen, the judgment is already being applied and that did not cause any market disturbance. where honey is produced in environments where there is no gmo cultivation, there is no problem. and in germany, for example, the supermarkets are already asking for proof that the honey is not gmo-free. if there is a sufficient distance between a gmo field and a hive, then that is accepted as sufficient evidence that there is no problem. it is therefore necessary to develop a good coexistence policy, to ensure that coexistence also takes into account bees, bees that sometimes fly 10 or 14 kilometres. so my call is: make sure there's a good coexistence policy. then the beekeepers will suffer no harm.

the agreement on the digital tachograph, which was concluded last may between negotiators from the commission, parliament and the member states, will be discussed today and finally adopted tomorrow. i would like to thank all those who have contributed to this, first of all, of course, the rapporteur, our good colleague, mrs ţicău, and all the shadow rapporteurs, for their good work. it is very important legislation which will be able to significantly promote the application of existing rules, usually also social rules of the game. the new legislation will equip new lorries with the new digital tachograph from 2015 onwards, which should contribute to safer road transport, a more social transport system and, of course, a fairer transport sector, as it will allow better organisation of the control of the rules that should lead to a level playing field for all. driving and rest times will be better controlled by making manipulation more difficult. the tachograph will be remotely controlled, so that time is not lost for the honest carrier, but inspectors will also be able to inspect more lorries. in addition, the tachograph is linked to the gps so that compliance with other rules, such as cabotage rules, can also be carried out more efficiently. if it fails, the responsibility will no longer be automatically placed on the driver, but in the first instance on the employer, who often puts pressure on the driver to play with the tachograph. on the other hand, small selfemployed workers within a radius of 100 km may also be exempted from the tachograph. this will reduce bureaucracy. in short, positive legislation, something that will help to put europe in a good light. of course, it is not a panacea. much will depend on how the member states implement all this.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to give special attention to relations between the european union and asean, which have often been unfairly placed behind relations between the european union and china, japan and india. this is despite the fact that the purchasing power and size of the asean economy are already comparable to those of china and that asean's political influence is increasing. the similarities between the european union and asean offer great potential for synergies and mutual learning. this report attempts to explore how the strengthening of economic relations can be accommodated within a more appropriate socio-political and institutional framework and relations. it also offers ideas on how to give a new dimension to bilateral relations between the regions. the evaluation and recommendations are presented in the context of the ambitious internal integration process under way within asean, the emergence of political powers and democratic challenges such as those faced by the next asean presidency, myanmar/burma, with its rapid transition and evolution towards democracy.
in writing. this report on rest and driving times in road transport is finally coming to fruition. the negotiations have dragged on for over a year and have been a tough one. the result is relatively satisfactory, as some crucial points have been incorporated in the final text. for example, driving times will be automatically recorded on the tachograph, together with the speed travelled. it is also important to us that it is not the driver but the employing company that will be held responsible for breaking this law. it is a pity that the entry into force of the directive is likely to take a long time, and in practice it may take up to five years. i hope that this kind of concrete legislation and action will restore confidence in europe. europe can no longer be seen as a threat. it's supposed to protect. this peace project is still gaining more than it is losing, but it urgently needs to be reversed in many respects. europe must be greener, more social and therefore more ecological. i fight for that every day.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. the tachograph is used in road transport to monitor compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods in the interests of road safety, decent working conditions for drivers and fair competition between transport undertakings. the proposed regulation, which will replace the regulation in force since 1985, aims to make fraud more difficult, to improve the enforcement of social legislation and to reduce the administrative burden by making full use of new technologies and introducing a number of new regulatory provisions.
in writing. in order to undertake public works and guarantee a range of goods and services, the state must maintain close relations with the private sector. the report therefore aims to regulate the award of public contracts by simplifying and streamlining procedures while maintaining maximum transparency, which will ensure fair competition. the report stresses the importance of also incorporating respect for a set of common social objectives such as respect for the environment, the fight against global warming, the better use of resources while simultaneously promoting innovation, employment and social inclusion. i am pleased to see that special attention has been paid to small and medium-sized enterprises in order to facilitate their access to this type of offer, in particular by simplifying administrative and bureaucratic formalities.
in writing. i would like to congratulate mr juvin and mr panzeri on their excellent work. i am convinced that a european legislative initiative on concessions is necessary. the lack of legal certainty, the persistence of over-the-counter contracts awarded in defiance of the main principles which have built the internal market of the european union and the legal patchwork existing at member state level in this field call for the establishment of a legislative framework at european level. however, this framework must respect a 'lightweight' approach which allows the establishment of clear, coherent, readable and effective rules. the rapporteur hopes that this objective has been achieved.
in writing. the revision of the two directives on public procurement is a major step forward for the european single market. the simplified procedures are intended to ensure the best possible use of public funds, which is crucial in times of tight budgetary resources. governments will also have to explain why they do not break up large contracts into smaller ones to provide more opportunities for smes and micro-enterprises. but the package goes beyond financial efficiency and economic leverage. quality and social value are also given prominent place. social and environmental criteria can now be taken into account by public authorities, and social services are even obliged to do so. governments may also reserve contracts for operators whose main objective is the social and professional integration of vulnerable workers, with a minimum percentage of such workers of only 30%. public procurement accounts for 19% of gdp in europe each year. this package of legislation will make this sector more transparent and fair.
in writing. i believe that the modernisation of the public procurement directives should strike a balance between simplifying the rules and ensuring sound and efficient procedures based on award criteria linked to innovation and sustainability, while also ensuring a higher participation of smes and making public procurement online more widespread. efforts should be made to exploit fully the potential of public procurement in the single market to promote sustainable growth, employment and social inclusion. given that public procurement represents a significant part of the economy (around 19% of the union's gdp), a successful overhaul and implementation of public procurement rules would make a significant contribution to the revival of investment in the real economy and to overcoming the crisis in the european economy. citizens expect every euro of public money to be spent in a useful, efficient and responsible way. this reform of public procurement was indispensable and will mark the daily lives of all the actors in our society.

in writing. the question and oral resolution tabled by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety aimed at keeping wildlife crime high on the political agenda of both the eu and the rest of the world. it is the fourth most important illegal activity, after drug trafficking, counterfeiting and human trafficking. it is strongly linked to organised crime and seriously threatens regional stability and security, human health and biodiversity. the revenues from trafficking in endangered species are estimated at between 18 and 26 billion euros per year. the eu is considered to be an important market and transit route for illegal wildlife trade. the resolution underlines the essential importance of a renewed and coordinated global response, based on the cites treaties and other laws and initiatives. it highlights the importance of strengthening political will at the highest level. the means of repression and criminal justice systems, both at national and international level, must be used more effectively and efficiently. the member states must allocate resources. moreover, appropriate criminal sanctions must be applied at all levels to avoid any gaps in the system.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. indeed, free movement is one of the european union's most cherished achievements. its strength lies in the commitment of the member states to fulfil their obligations and to respect the fundamental rights of the union. the four freedoms of movement of workers, capital, services and goods are guaranteed by the treaties, as they have led to the completion of the single market. these freedoms cannot be separated or evaluated individually. together, they form the foundations of the european project. in some member states there is a debate on the possibility of restricting the fundamental right to free movement for romanian and bulgarian workers. in the united kingdom, restrictions on the access of polish workers to the british social security system have recently been announced. member states which have expressed criticism of the free movement of workers and raised publicly the issue of maintaining or imposing new restrictions on citizens of other eu member states have failed to provide concrete data to support their position.

in writing. i voted in favour of the text. there is considerable debate in the kimberley process on how to strengthen the system. the commission is now considering the possibility of launching initiatives on 'conflict minerals' to address issues such as the origin of minerals, security of supply, supply chain transparency and good governance; the kimberley process should serve as a model for these initiatives. it is also important that the commission draws lessons from its experience in other areas and continues to invest in the kimberley process in order to encourage csr practices and the establishment of peer review mechanisms among the states participating in the process. in accordance with the provisions of the lisbon treaty, parliament must be informed fully and without delay of any developments at any stage of the proceedings, in particular with regard to this important commercial matter.
in writing. any territorial entity wishing to join the process and willing to respect and implement it effectively should be welcomed. the rapporteur therefore welcomes the commission's ingenious solution, which proposes to include greenland in the eu certification system as an overseas country and territory. we hope that parliament will support the adoption of a rapid solution to this problem. the specific amendments proposed by the commission serve precisely this purpose. the rapporteur therefore intends to support these proposals without any amendments.
in writing. i see no objection to this, so i voted in favour of this amendment to regulation (eu) no 260/2012 as regards the migration to a european system of credit transfers and direct debits.
in writing. the cape town agreement, which aims to improve the safety of fishing vessels, was reached at a conference organised by the international maritime organisation in october 2012. due to the regional nature of the european union and the absence of a clause recognising regional economic integration organisations, the union cannot be a contracting party. this is all the more problematic as the content of the agreement falls within the exclusive competence of the european union. the report thus seeks to give the member states of the union the opportunity to sign this agreement in the name of the community interest. although i welcome this proposal because it seems to me essential that europeans are bound by this international agreement , i remain somewhat bitter because of the impossibility for the european union to sign on its own behalf an international agreement which falls within its own competence.
in writing. i support the current european standards, which apply not only to fishing vessels flying the flag of a member state but also to fishing vessels flying the flag of a third country that are operating in the internal or territorial waters of a member state or that land their catch in a member state port. they ensure that all vessels are subject to a common safety regime and guarantee fair competition in union waters. i also hope that the cape town agreement, when it comes into force, will not only contribute to the safety of fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more, but will also set the first milestones in addressing the problems associated with smaller vessels, which make up the majority of fishing vessels. in 2007, the overwhelming majority of the 89 000 fishing vessels registered in the union were less than 18 metres long (eusta 09).
in writing. the legislation of the european union is complex and extensive and often plays a decisive role in the lives of european citizens. however, in many cases, such as directives, eu legislation must first be transposed into the national law of each member state. on the other hand, eu regulations are directly applicable in domestic law and must therefore be taken into account by all european citizens. although this hierarchy of standards may seem difficult to understand, it is essential that union law is applied and respected throughout the union. the rule of law also applies at european level. however, as the commission report shows, in many cases the application of european law is not respected within the time limits. it is thus clear that directives are not always transposed into national legislation in time. in the face of this worrying record, there is reason to fear that the commission does not have sufficiently effective tools to monitor effectively the application of eu law in europe and to systematically distinguish shortcomings in the member states.
in writing. i am in favour of this text. as a reminder, according to the european parliament's legal service, the eu pilot online platform, which is used by the member states and the commission to clarify the factual and legal framework of problems relating to the application of union law, has no legal status and, in accordance with the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the commission, the commission is required to provide parliament with summary information on all infringement procedures, including on a case-by-case basis, as from the letter of formal notice, and may, in the context of the eu pilot project, refuse access only to personal data.
in writing. mr soffritti argues that the remarks made by lara comi in his regard during that debate are damaging to his reputation and has therefore lodged a complaint for aggravated defamation within the meaning of the second and third paragraphs of article 595 of the italian penal code and article 30 of law 223 of 6 august 1990. at the same time, mr soffriti served lara comi with a summons to appear before the court of ferrara to settle the damage allegedly caused to the civilian. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, was adopted on the basis of the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs. i agree with the latter.
in writing. the present case fulfils the conditions for the application of article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union. it is true that allegedly slanderous statements could, in principle, fall within the scope of the absolute immunity provided for in article 8 of the protocol. however, the court of justice has clearly defined the scope of this provision by holding that 'a statement made by a member of the european parliament outside the european parliament which has given rise to criminal proceedings in his member state of origin for the offence of slander constitutes an opinion expressed in the exercise of parliamentary functions falling within the immunity provided for in this provision only where that statement corresponds to a subjective assessment which has a direct and obvious link with the exercise of such functions'. similarly, the court has recently recalled its case-law in gollnisch, namely that a member's opinion can only be covered by immunity established on the basis of eu law if it was issued 'in the exercise of [his] duties', thus implying the requirement of a link between the opinion expressed and parliamentary duties. this link must be direct and obvious.
in writing. the mobility of 12 million union citizens who study, work or live in a member state of which they are not nationals is not only a reality but also a fundamental right, recognised as early as the treaty of rome in 1957. in its resolution on the stockholm programme 2009, the european parliament called for a 'simple and autonomous european system for the abolition of the obligation to obtain the legalisation of acts', respecting the rights enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights by the union and the 'justice for growth' policy. it was therefore time to simplify the acceptance of certain public documents, such as identity cards, diplomas, proof of disability, tax and social security documents. the free movement of persons, a pillar of the single market contributing to the union's economic growth, is undoubtedly one of the great successes of european integration which must continue to be encouraged and supported.
in writing. this text is a real simplification for the citizen. in 2011, eurostat estimated that around 12 million eu citizens were living outside their country of origin, in another eu country. many others are temporarily staying in another eu country to study, work or simply to spend their holidays. all these people may at some time be in contact with the administrative authorities of the state in which they are staying: tourists with the health system, students with the administrative services of universities, workers with the tax authorities and social security, etc. for citizens of another member state, this contact is often synonymous with bureaucratic efforts and obstacles. even if they are fluent in the language of the administration, they are not familiar with, for example, local administrative practices.

in writing. it can be said that in periods of economic growth and low unemployment, labour is drawn from agriculture, hence an acceleration in the implementation of technologies that reduce labour requirements and change agricultural structures. in contrast, in times of economic recession, such as the one currently affecting the southern eu member states, labour is reabsorbed into agriculture, which serves as a buffer against the level of unemployment in the cities. from an economic point of view this is a positive situation, but if the scale of migration from the countryside and agriculture due to the replacement of labour by capital is large and sustainable, this phenomenon can lead to a strengthening of the depopulation situation and, consequently, to the withering away of the countryside and the places of life in rural areas.

member of the commission. - mr president, i would like to make three points. for those of us who have attended this debate in parliament, and even more so for the rapporteur, i hope that what is in this report can be the common denominator of this parliament tomorrow. it is not just that we can hear that this is a very split parliament, but it is also clear that the split goes down into party groups and into national delegations, which shows how challenging this has become. my second point is yes, it is true, europe today accounts for around 11% of global emissions, but when you account for 11% of global emissions that does not mean that you do not have a responsibility to deliver your fair contribution to the international table. but that is not the only reason why the commission has presented this package. at present, europe is the region of the world most dependent on imported fossil fuels. that is why it makes a lot of sense – economic sense, as well as sense when it comes to competitiveness and jobs – that we get a better energy policy for europe, that we focus more on efficiency, on renewables and on alternative sources. it is somehow strange that those who are so preoccupied with the energy bills of european citizens – as many of us are – that they never make a point of the more than eur 500 billion that the eu’s member states each year pour into putin’s russia and the different regimes in the middle east and elsewhere from which we import our fossil fuels? there are more reasons than just the international climate negotiations why we should address these kinds of issues, and if you read the package that we presented from the commission it is clear that this is one aspect; but the other aspects are also very much present. my third point is to bas eickhout, who said that it is difficult to combine being ambitious and being realistic. well, it might be difficult to combine, but to do exactly that – combining what is ambitious with what is realistic – is basically what politics is all about. is 40% domestic ambitious? we had 20% up to 2020. if all member states do everything they say they plan to do, we could reach 23/24. one quarter of that will come through offsetting. now we are saying that without offsetting we are going to 40% in the following decade. i just have to say that i am not sure that those who say this is not ambitious have really grasped how challenging this is going to be. i also have to say in this parliament that in the commission we have not heard one government arguing in favour of more than 40% domestic. not one. whereas we have heard several argue in favour of less. that is how it looks, that is the political picture, and i would only say to those of us who want ambition, including ambition in fighting climate change, that the test is whether we can also get it through, so that europe can very soon send a signal to the world and play the role that we must play if the world is to try to get an international framework to combat climate change in place by 2015. it would be very helpful if tomorrow this parliament adopted the report that we have been discussing today.
member of the commission. - mr president, i have to go. i am very grateful for the many comments and also for the constructive and critical suggestions. i want to go into three very shortly. it doesn't seem clear whether we need one target or three or two. the first is clear: the reduction of co2 emissions. i think there are also a lot of implications for renewable energy and energy efficiency. but we should continue to pursue an independent energy efficiency policy and not just rely on the fact that reducing co2 emissions automatically leads to less energy waste, less energy consumption and more accurate energy use. the energy efficiency label should be a label for the european strategy for the next decade. we shall have to debate in the autumn whether we should declare a binding target or set out various measures, whether we should put energy intensity in the foreground or whether we should set absolute figures for energy consumption. but to let the energy efficiency directive 2020 expire and to blame everything on the co2 reduction would be too little for me. the same applies to renewable energy sources. when you say co2 reductions, you're making a real claim. i would like to make it clear that we, as the commission, are neutral in relation to nuclear energy. we are sure that in the next decade, in the next decades, nuclear power will play a role in the european electricity mix - from 28% today in the eu-28, in ten, twenty years in any case, much more than 20%, i estimate even more than 25%. it is only if we have no targets for renewable energy in addition to co2 emissions reduction and, conversely, nuclear power receives indirect guarantees through feed-in tariffs that the balance between two equally emission-friendly but completely opposite technologies - nuclear power and renewable energy sources - does not seem to me to be maintained. that is why i am in favour of continuing our policy on renewable energies with a binding target at european level. mr leinen said that was not ambitious. but at least 27%, if you look at all the sectors - transport, heating, electricity - will only be achievable if we produce at least 45% renewable energy in the electricity sector - at least 45%! that means that in our future electricity mix, almost half will come from wind, solar, geothermal, biomass and hydropower. that's ambitious! i would argue that if we set this value, europe will be on track to produce more storm renewably than any other continent in the world. to get acceptance for this, we need instruments. that is why mr leinen was right when he said that we need better governance. the european budget is helping to do this. we are promoting renewable energy through expertise and analysis, through research, through funding, through networks and infrastructure. in conclusion, i believe that we also need a european support system. a european system for the timely and degressive marketing and promotion of renewable energy. but not 28 separate times, but once european. i believe that's part of it. the last point: the subject of nuclear energy and the united kingdom was raised. we will examine this without prejudice. we want the single market to be as strong as possible. security of supply is even more important than the single market. so, avoiding blackouts, having a secure power supply, is paramount. but we are currently looking at whether there are other ways of maintaining security of supply in the uk with new investment and nuclear not necessarily requiring a feed-in tariff for 35 years. and since this is the first comparable case that would certainly trigger follow-up requests in the united kingdom, hungary, poland and other countries, it is being examined particularly thoroughly. i am happy to be in contact with the interested members of the house so that our debate and that of mr almunia on the question of the internal market and security of supply, on the example of the united kingdom, will be able to reach the right conclusion.
the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. of course, we remain divided, but we knew that from the beginning. i would like to return to something that i think is important. no, the objective of this climate and energy framework is not just to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. no, i'm not going. there's more to it than that. i agree with mr chris davies that we need to promote a low-carbon, low-cost economy. but what is meant by low-carbon and low-cost economy is also meant by "new technologies, innovation, employment". and do you think that a single greenhouse gas reduction target will address these challenges? what about jobs, new technology, innovation? no, make no mistake about it. i really believe that the three-pronged approach has many and varied benefits. i would like to stress that the energy efficiency criterion is the most important in terms of its contribution to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. a single target of 40% energy efficiency by 2030 would allow us to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions by 50% and achieve a 35% share of renewable energy in our energy production without any additional measures. i don't have one. the figures are 40, 50 or 60 per cent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. i don't want to get into a numbers battle. i'm not thinking, "who's going to say it better?" i think we need to be ambitious, but clearly realistic. for my part, i continue to promote the 40% target in the roadmap for 2050. i will simply conclude by saying that 2030 is not tomorrow, but that we must have a short-term, medium-term and long-term vision. tomorrow, when you vote, please don't throw the baby out with the bath water! have a vision that is perhaps a little less ideological, but much more pragmatic!

president, vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, we are discussing today a very important matter which is helping our european citizens in a very concrete way and is also bringing europe into the limelight in a positive way, namely the matter of passenger rights. the 2004 regulation required a major facelift due to the many loopholes in the legislation, the different interpretations given to it and the judgments of the court of justice. i think that under the leadership of my colleague, rapporteur bach, and with the help of the shadow rapporteurs and others, we have come to a clearer and better legislation. the right to compensation for delays, not just cancellations, is an important development. in this context, it is of course essential to define very clearly what is meant by 'exceptional circumstances'. and that's well covered in the legislation. but perhaps even more important is that people are helped when they're in trouble, when they're facing problems. then it's how they're informed if something goes wrong. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. these kinds of things are being recorded much more clearly now. and i think that's an important step forward. in short, if we look at the commission's proposal and certainly at the existing regulation, we can say that parliament has done an excellent job. we have a very good basis to work on. the ball is now in the council's court and we hope that they will adopt the pro-passenger attitude that we have been advocating.

madam president, article 6.2 concerns the three trigger points from which a passenger is entitled to get compensation after a delay. to avoid confusion, the first one should cover all intra-european flights and therefore we need to replace the figure 2 500 kilometres by 3 500 kilometres. article 6.2(a) would therefore read as follows: ‘three hours or more after the scheduled time of arrival for all journeys of 3 500 kilometres or less’. obviously, article 6.2(b) would be amended accordingly. i take it that the rapporteur agrees with this and i thank him for his indulgence.
in writing. i voted for this text, of course. we strongly encourage member states to decouple migration policies from health, education and prosecution of crimes against undocumented migrants. access to basic health care and education and protection of physical integrity are fundamental rights, and undocumented migrants are entitled to them regardless of their legal status or residence. thus, migrants should be able to access these basic services and report abusers to the police without fear of arrest and deportation.
in writing. for the first time since the treaty of lisbon, we are adopting common rules on legal immigration. by adopting the report on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of seasonal employment in the union, we wanted to harmonise the conditions of entry and residence and the rights of more than 100 000 seasonal workers per year. they will enjoy better living and working conditions, including social protection, adequate housing and a minimum wage. this report, based on solidarity between member states and cooperation with third countries, will make it possible to manage migration flows more soundly, in the interests not only of the host countries but also of the countries of origin and of the migrants themselves.
in writing. - despite the fact that we had a more ambitious content in mind for this directive, i voted for it because it represents a first major step (not least for the council) in a legal migration scheme for (often low-skilled) seasonal workers. the positive aspects are a clear definition of seasonal work, a good delimitation of the scope and clear rules on residence, visas and working conditions with the right to equal treatment. for example, employers will have to create the same working conditions as for local workers in terms of working hours, leave and safety conditions at work. seasonal workers have the same right to strike, the same access to services and the same pension rights. training and education is a right, although member states may limit it to training linked to specific work activities. it is also important that employers who do not respect these agreements can be sanctioned. in the case of subcontracting, the main contractor is also responsible. finally, it is stated that the cost of accommodation should not be excessive in relation to the net income and the quality of the accommodation. in addition, the rent cannot be automatically deducted from the income and a separate lease must be drawn up. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied.
in writing. the proposed directive is an integral part of a package of measures on legal migration (alongside the rules on intra-corporate transfers, students, researchers and au pairs, which are yet to be agreed). the s&d group welcomes the fact that our negotiator, mr claude moraes, was able to secure agreement on the first legal migration instrument geared towards low-skilled and low-wage jobs, and that this agreement will be the first part of the 'package' on legal migration to be adopted. as always, the text presented at first reading is a compromise, but it incorporates many significant advances for the european parliament in general and for the s&d group in particular.

in writing. the conclusion of this protocol is positive in more than one respect: in addition to strengthening the links between the union and gabon, it introduces new control instruments in the fight against illegal fishing (through the establishment of a satellite vessel monitoring system and a new electronic communication system); it is in line with a sustainable development policy, in accordance with the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icsat); finally, it allows the development of the workforce along the coast by providing aid to coastal communities and small freezing and processing enterprises. in practical terms, while this agreement is beneficial for gabon, it is also beneficial for the union by giving 27 purse seiners and 8 reelers the opportunity to fish for tuna and other highly migratory species in gabon's exclusive economic zone (eez) for a reference tonnage of 20 000 tonnes per year, compared with 11 000 previously.

in writing. with global warming, greenland, an overseas country and territory (oct), is becoming a strategic and economic challenge for many powers in search of new natural resources and new waterways. close to the union, it is coveted by neighbouring countries such as norway, russia and canada, as well as countries such as china. according to the usgs, the arctic has estimated potential reserves of 13% of the world's oil and 30% of the world's natural gas, or 80 000 billion cubic metres of gas and 200 billion barrels of oil. the gradual thawing of the arctic also makes it easier to navigate for much of the year, opening up the possibility of a viable sea corridor between europe, asia and the americas. in this context, it was time to establish a new partnership that would help diversify its economy in a sustainable way.

in writing. storm tides, forest fires, river floods and flash floods are among the main risks of natural disasters in europe. the damage caused by these disasters is not only human but also economic. in order to avoid paying a price in human, environmental and economic lives, we must pay greater attention to precautionary measures and, consequently, improve prevention. as kristalina georgieva, commissioner for humanitarian aid and crisis response, said, "well-designed insurance policies can be a market-based instrument to discourage risky behaviour, raise awareness and integrate disaster prevention into economic and financial decisions".

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the 'exceptional circumstances' interpreted at the discretion of the airlines are clarified, as are the rules on compensation. compensation for 3 hours delay for an intra-european flight and 5 hours for a non-eu flight could be provided and a point of contact would have to be provided by the airlines to assist passengers and inform them within 30 minutes of the scheduled departure time of the aircraft. also, you're done taking passengers hostage by locking them for over two hours in a plane stuck on the tarmac. other changes proposed by parliament include the possibility of using the return flight without having to take the outward flight and the need to hide personal effects or to stack them in one piece of hand luggage. all these rights could soon become a reality - if the council and the commission, which are closer to industry, follow the european parliament! i didn't win!
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in respect of the carriage of goods by air. the commission proposal is a revision of existing legislation on air passenger rights and is mainly geared to the interests of airlines and airports. the commission proposal would only allow passengers to be compensated if their flight is delayed by at least five hours, whereas the european court of justice has recently ruled that passengers should be compensated for three hours of delay. the european parliament follows this ruling and proposes compensation for three hours' delay, depending on the distance. the definition of 'extraordinary circumstances', which is used by airlines to avoid compensation, is also narrowed. passengers will be insured so that they do not lose their rights when airlines go bankrupt. air carriers will have to demonstrate that they have taken sufficient measures to compensate passengers for cancellation of their flights in the event of bankruptcy. the commission has also proposed the creation of an independent mediation body to mediate in civil-passenger disputes. these are all advantages for the passenger and that is why i am voting in favour.

on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, in the past few weeks we have made enough statements and issued enough press releases about ukraine, and made enough speeches also in ukraine but, commissioner füle, what i do not see is a credible strategy on ukraine. i do not see what i would call an action-based strategy capable of really changing things in ukraine and stopping the violence. such a strategy can, however, be put forward and it should contain three elements. the first element, to put it somewhat bluntly, is to load the gun. we have to prepare a number of target sanctions against the regime and against individual members of the regime. i am thinking, for example, of banning individuals from travelling to europe, restricting their visas and, most importantly, freezing their assets. the last of these, the freezing of assets, is the most crucial. the three sanctions, naturally, must go hand in hand with positive measures towards ukraine: a visa-free regime for all ordinary ukrainians, for example. that is the first thing to do. are we preparing such sanctions – yes, or no? for the greens/efa group mr president, mr minister, mr barroso, you are too modest. i think you are being too modest because you are telling us that we are perhaps seeing the first signs of an end to the crisis; you are being too modest because growth is back. it is in a massive way. of course, it is the growth of debt, unemployment, inequality, poverty, it is the growth - mr swoboda said it - of disease, infant mortality. but growth is back. corien, i heard you when you said that we were in an untenable situation and that it's normal that the effort hurts. you are right: we were in an unsustainable situation in the crisis countries, as in the rest of europe. the question is, who is paying for the effort today? does the distribution of efforts correspond to the distribution of responsibilities for the crisis? are the efforts being distributed fairly? the answer is obviously no, and that is what i think justifies the revolt of a large part of our citizens, who say that the way out of the crisis is obviously pleasant for some and very unpleasant and unbearable for others. let's not make a mistake! mr rehn, we are strong supporters of the european semester and of the coordination of economic and social policies within the european union. the semester is an indispensable tool. nevertheless, you have made it an instrument which is directed exclusively at two objectives: the reduction of public expenditure and the reduction of the so-called labour costs, that is to say wages and social protection. do you seriously think that this is how we are going to get europe out of the crisis? - i'm the reporter. - i think i am entrapping an open door when i say that we in europe have been through and are still going through the worst economic crisis since the second world war. i think that the debate today also shows that we are not out of the crisis yet, that there is still more work to be done. that is also the message of my report on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs. the work is not done! it would therefore be a great pity if the commission or some member states thought that we had arrived at that moment and that the reform packages still to be implemented and the savings and reforms still to be achieved could now be put on the back burner. the very fragile economic recovery we are witnessing today shows that we must go further down the road we have taken. we must continue to implement these reform packages. this will be crucial to stimulating economic growth and job creation. my report therefore clearly sets out the tasks that still lie ahead. firstly, there are a number of tasks at european level. it is quite clear that we must also do everything we can at european level to increase our competitiveness. both the member states and the european union as a whole must remain competitive and seek to conquer new export markets in order to create the growth needed to generate prosperity internally. this will have to be done through structural reforms in the labour market, in the pension system, in social security, not to organise social breakdown but precisely to offer the next generation the prospect of a social security as we european union, are needed to make the best use of the european funds. i am thinking of investments in research and development, horizon 2020, research and infrastructure, investments to make our generate the necessary sustainable jobs and long-term growth. the key to this is, of course, democracy and democratic control of the whole process. my report is very clear on this point too. that work is not finished either! we will also have to take steps to ensure that everything that happens here in the european parliament and all the proposals of the european commission are examined here in the european parliament. the community method is, of course, the appropriate method for this purpose. we must therefore ensure that all programmes proposed by the troika, for example, are submitted to parliament for democratic scrutiny. the european parliament is also the place where everything related to the european stability mechanism can be examined, because it is here that the democratic control and the democratic legitimacy of the commission to take these steps are based. we must also ensure that what we agree here is actually implemented. ladies and gentlemen, it is of course still a very difficult economic period that we are going through today, but the worst thing we can do now is to rest on our laurels and no longer think and look ahead. it is impossible to build a social paradise on an economic graveyard. so first of all we must get our economy back on track, encourage private investment, do everything possible on the public side to invest in education, development, research and transport infrastructure so that our economy can grow again and generate the necessary jobs and prosperity for our citizens.
mr president, commissioner, i will of course dwell on the cofferati report by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, stressing in particular that the protection of citizens' rights, whether as consumers or as citizens, is fundamental, also for workers. we must build trust in this single market and encourage responsible behaviour. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's new rules on the protection of personal data, in particular the new rules on the protection of personal data. hence the importance of following the transposition. let me also welcome the report by mr gutierrez prieto on the quality of employment, because we have spoken a lot about growth and we are right to talk about returning to growth, but growth has no meaning if we do not talk about how it is redistributed. reducing inequalities is fundamental in europe. i'll take an example from outside europe: qatar [nbsp]6.6[nbsp]% growth in 2012[nbsp], which is based on a system of slave labor and where, already, 850[nbsp] foreign workers have died on the construction sites of the future and shameful world cup[nbsp]2022. this example will have shown that we must of course return to growth, but that it must be shared and accompanied by quality jobs and fundamental respect for those who participate in it, that is to say, the workers.
mr president, commissioner, the reports of my colleagues - and i welcome them - must help to assert the role of parliament in the european semester process. their recommendations should be taken into account. i would stress the need for growth in europe, not exclusive austerity. the fact that all member states must be involved in reducing economic imbalances, including those with trade surpluses; or the fact that the existence of a social scoreboard is a step forward, but that it must be binding in order to be useful. in social matters, the european semester should be a catalyst, not for the dismantling of the social protection system but for the fight against poverty, with decent wages and incomes throughout europe that allow the strengthening of the purchasing power of citizens, to ensure quality employment, in particular through a strengthened social dialogue, and to invest in youth, in particular through the youth guarantee, with sufficient budgetary means. if we do not change our approach, particularly in these areas, we shall not regain the confidence of the citizens.
rapporteur. - mr president, i want to thank, first of all, all the colleagues who have worked on this report. both in the committee on economic and monetary affairs and in the committee on employment and social affairs we found a very good, a very strong and a very clear compromise which also sends a very clear signal to the council and to the commission. i must say after listening to the debate that i do not think that the european semester is from the right or from the left. i think that we, as the european parliament, should take up our role in this process much more maybe than we do today. we have of course, after the very difficult economic situation, taken a road ahead, also supported by this parliament: a road of reducing deficits and balancing budgets; a road of implementing economic reform; a road of modernising social protection; but also a road of investing in education, research and development. we cannot go back and restore the mistakes which were made at the start and the onset of the creation of the euro. but i do feel that we must do our utmost – and maybe it is the task of our generation – to make sure that we correct the mistakes and take a clear path forward. my report and the report by mr[nbsp ]gutiérrez prieto start this process and provide a clear path forward: a combination of more democratic accountability, a combination of solidarity with conditionality and clear responsibilities, and also more room for private investment, to boost investment and to improve entrepreneurship and create jobs and growth. these reforms are not, of course, always pleasant but it is also our job as politicians to have the courage to defend the road taken and the benefits it will bring in the long term. this is, i think, our job as politicians and also the job of our generation. we could not continue with business as usual. we could not continue along the road that was taken 20 years ago, so it is now time for a new path. i think that with more democratic control – we are here in the european parliament, the centre of european democracy – that if we can take a step forward here, if we can continue along the path that we have followed, we will reconnect with economic growth, we will reconnect with job creation and we can offer the young generation of europe a future.
the social scoreboard is included for the first time in the annual growth survey and thus in the european semester. the social scoreboard is being put forward by the european commission as a concrete step towards strengthening the social dimension of emu. this should not be used as a 'sweetener' to counter the difficult questions of a social europe. i want to make it clear that a social scoreboard like this only makes sense if it also links actions. after all, what is the point of mapping social indicators and then not doing anything about them? the european commission has been taking stock of the macroeconomic indicators of the member states for some time. these form the basis for strict budgetary objectives imposed on member states. as long as the european commission imposes binding macroeconomic objectives on the member states but only accepts social objectives on a voluntary basis, we shall never be able to revive the european union. my plea is therefore simple and clear: no enforceable budgetary objectives or strict macroeconomic objectives without these being balanced by enforceable social objectives. economic measures on an equal footing with social measures. this is the only way to achieve the social revival of europe.

in writing. - this report is welcome, as it aims to increase the efficiency and sustainability of passenger cars, thereby promoting both a low-carbon economy and sustainable growth, and reducing the eu's dependence on oil. the 2020 target of 95 g co2/km should be maintained, as the industry should be given appropriate planning and investment certainty. however, i was not in favour of a more far-reaching 2025 target. however, given that the guidance is set at between 68 and 78[nbsp]g co2/km, the commission has a certain margin of discretion. this flexibility is needed in setting the emission standards it requires in order not to stand in the way of a more rapid and sustainable development of vehicles. i also welcome the continuation of the incentives, because they provide incentives for the use of sustainable technologies. however, the creation of the appropriate infrastructure must also be considered in this context, because what is the use of an electric car if there are very few charging points? setting sustainable but above all realistic targets for new cars will strengthen europe's research and innovation base and thus help to counter the relocation of production sites and the associated job losses in europe.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the original proposal would have allowed an average passenger car to emit between 68 and 78g co2 per km after 2025. however, this was not accepted by the representatives of the member states. they got the christian democrat rapporteur to agree to a maximum of 95g co2 emissions per km by 2020. it is even more unimaginable that the five per cent of the most polluting vehicles have a back door to avoid the low-level commitments. i regret that some member states still do not realise that strong climate policy and technological innovation go hand in hand. if we in the european union do not have the political courage to force the car industry to implement environmental reforms, who will? i voted against this proposal because nature and consumers are paying the price for this weak compromise.
in writing. eu legislation on this subject, adopted in 2009, sets mandatory emission reduction targets for new cars. it aims to increase these emissions from the average of 130 grams of co2 per kilometre observed between 2012 and 2015 to 95g/km by 2020. the commission proposal sets out how this target will be achieved by 2020. reducing co2 emissions from cars is good for consumers and the environment. it allows a reduction in fuel consumption and the maintenance of the competitive advantage of the european automobile industry on the world market.
in writing. the growing importance of the internal market requires modern european legislation to enable our businesses to remain competitive. in addition, even if traders do not wish to have their marks protected at union level, they must be able to enjoy legal certainty when registering their marks. it was therefore necessary to harmonise certain aspects of national procedures and to impose a system of cooperation between national offices and the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim). this constant effort to reduce disparities between the laws of the member states of the union will further reduce the obstacles to the free movement of goods and services and, consequently, to any obstacle to free competition within the internal market. i welcome this proposal which limits the divergences between the provisions of the existing regulatory framework and improves cooperation between the trademark systems. this new legislation will also help us to fight counterfeiting more effectively.
in writing. the reform of the community trade mark comes at a time when eu customs authorities are reporting massive infringements of intellectual property rules, particularly with regard to counterfeiting and new strategies for infiltrating borders. in these circumstances, the eu must take firm measures to protect its citizens from counterfeiting. a trademark is an intellectual property instrument with a renewable 10-year validity, which guarantees the origin of goods and services. this reduces safety and health risks for consumers. the content of the package in question is the subject of a broad consensus among the political groups. the main elements are related to goods in transit, small consignments, generic medicines, mediation, trademark rights, legitimate use of trademarks and the right of individuals to take legal action in the event of infringement.
in writing. drug trafficking, human trafficking, arms trafficking and corruption can only be dismantled by the establishment of strong and effective transnational rules that effectively combat crossborder crime and the huge profits it generates. it was urgent to establish common rules on the freezing and confiscation of the assets of organised crime groups, because only in this way will we be able to seize their profits and put an end to their sources of funding. i regret, however, that the united kingdom and denmark are not bound by the directive, thus weakening the european system.
in writing. right after the decision with respect to the ukrainian leaders, chance does things well. the european parliament has long called on the commission to propose new legislation on confiscation. in its own-initiative report adopted in october 2011, parliament stressed in particular the need for new rules on the effective use of extended confiscation and confiscation without conviction, rules allowing for the confiscation of assets transferred to third parties. parliament also called for the introduction into national systems of instruments to alleviate the burden of proof in criminal, civil or tax law as regards the origin of assets held by a person convicted of an offence related to organised crime.

in writing. the role of europol is fundamental in the fight against international crime and money laundering. however, due to its considerable potential and the processing of many sensitive data, the agency requires special attention from policy-makers in order to avoid any kind of overload. as an advocate of personal data protection, i welcome this balanced report which aims to limit the agency's processing of private data as much as possible without compromising its effectiveness. sensitive information will thus be processed only by a limited number of identified staff with specific objectives which are themselves defined in advance.
in writing. crime is the fifth most important concern of european citizens, far behind unemployment, the economic situation or the decline in purchasing power. but in the majority of the 28 member states, the crisis is accompanied by a general increase in crime. that is why this report on europol, the european police office in the hague, is timely. it is clear that the missions of the 600 europol staff must be strengthened and the exchange of information between national police authorities facilitated. what is more, europol has been responsible for a number of investigations: it has helped the commission to trace the chain from horse meat fraud. this justifies a larger budget than the current 83 million euro. another problem identified was cybercrime. according to a recent eurobarometer, 12% of european internet users have had their email or website hacked and 7% have been victims of credit card fraud. again, the new european cybercrime centre at europol will need to be better equipped to develop real eu expertise in the fight against cybercrime.
in writing. the main aims of this regulation are to establish the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training (europol), to repeal decision 2009/371/jha and to align it with the lisbon treaty by increasing its accountability. the proposal also aims to strengthen the democratic governance and parliamentary oversight of europol, both at european and national level. the european parliament and national parliaments will receive annual activity reports and balance sheets. they will also receive information on annual and multiannual programmes, risk assessments, policy analyses and general situation reports. the proposal strengthens and clarifies the data protection regime: giving the european data protection supervisor (edps) general supervision of europol's processing of personal data; strengthening the rights of access to personal data; clarifying the use of personal data and introducing the necessary safeguards.
in writing. as a humanist and universalist, i can only welcome the adoption of such a report which aims to encourage the temporary arrival in europe of scientific researchers, students, people in paid and unpaid training, volunteers and au pairs from third countries. i am convinced that this will facilitate the exchange of knowledge and know-how, which is one of the undeniable drivers of competitiveness. as the report points out, a clear legal framework is essential in order to avoid situations of exploitation and undeclared work. the loss of competitiveness and the ageing of the population are major challenges for europeans to address. this report is a start to the response but it must be part of a much broader approach which includes managed and humanized immigration.
in writing. - this revision of the legislation integrates and clarifies the conditions and procedures for the residence in the european union of students and researchers from third countries. two existing directives are integrated into a new one and the framework is extended to include paid traineeships and au pairs. this creates clarity and finally provides a legal status for au pairs and also for paid trainees. the new directive sets out the conditions for applicants for residence and also lays down rules for the member states on the processing of the application (including a time limit and transparency). it thus provides for rights and obligations both for third-country nationals wishing to reside in the european union and for the european member states dealing with these applications. this is to prevent arbitrariness, facilitate the processing of residence applications and strengthen the rights of foreign students, researchers, trainees and au pairs. researchers, students and trainees will also be able to travel within european member states. and the new directive introduces the possibility for researchers and students to stay temporarily after finishing their research or studies to look for work or start a business. these amendments are a good thing, i vote for them.
in writing. this report concerns a proposal for a directive put forward by the commission on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, training, voluntary work and pair work. it is an integral part of a european package of legal migration instruments, which includes the recently adopted directive on seasonal workers and the directive on intra-group posting. it is a question of developing a rational and positive approach to migration in general. this report reinforces the commission's proposal to make the eu more attractive to migrants from third countries. the commission is also proposing that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of certain substances and preparations.
in writing. the commission's approach is to make the corps complementary to existing structures and organisations, in order to avoid duplication of effort. the corps' actions must be guided by humanitarian principles (european consensus on humanitarian aid), even though some humanitarian partners have expressed doubts about the initiative, in particular its true added value and funding. the preparation of the report has allowed lessons to be learned from the various pilot projects carried out or in progress related to the proposal. eu aid volunteers will therefore only be deployed in humanitarian aid operations in third countries in response to man-made crises or natural disasters, and never in the event of armed conflict or internal unrest. once the programme is launched, a consultative forum will be set up, bringing together representatives of the commission, eu countries and sending and hosting organisations.

in writing. today's vote is purely technical and does not call into question the acquis generated on 22 may 2012, the day when the council and the european parliament adopted regulation (eu) no[nbsp]528/2012 on biocidal products. legislation based on better harmonisation of marketing rules but above all aiming at a high level of protection of human health and the environment. for example, carcinogenic, mutagenic and reproductive toxic (cmr) or endocrine disrupting active substances are excluded. for example, formaldehyde, one of the most dangerous pollutants, has been banned from biocidal uses: human hygiene products, disinfectants for areas in contact with food, disinfectants for drinking water, anti-fouling products. but much remains to be done, and to paraphrase a french expert: "today, many biocidal products are still on the market without evaluation...: in the long run, this regulation is intended to sort out products that are available to mr and mrs all-the-world, with minimal labelling". it is therefore up to europe and the national authorities to take the necessary steps to ensure that highly toxic biocides are no longer placed on the european market.

i cannot accept that this money can go into the pockets of my competitor – though of course it can go to the budget or infrastructure manager. the issue of how to have a transparent and fair flow of money between the infrastructure and operators must be solved. we do not just advocate the dismantling of a vertical company. we are also trying to create, proposing to create a certain system to produce this transparency. so if we have another solution whereby every country has as single integrated railway company, how can we then organise the cross-border movement of trains? vice-president of the commission. - mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate ms[nbsp ]de veyrac, as rapporteur, and the shadow rapporteurs for their valuable input and contribution to the discussions, and, more generally, parliament as well, for its strong support for the objectives of the commission proposal. i am pleased that an agreement has been found with the council on the text. the commission fully supports the compromise arrived at by the co-legislators. the european union must be the world’s leading region for aviation safety. parliament, the member states and the commission have worked collectively in that direction over past years. however, we should not stop there. with air traffic expected to increase in future decades, our recent good safety record could be followed by more accidents and fatalities. we therefore have a responsibility to provide a safety system that is more proactive and improves aviation safety even further. this regulation is a cornerstone for a modern approach to safety policy that seeks to improve safety further – by learning not only from accidents but also from small incidents and occurrences, even if they have not been the cause of serious consequences in themselves. by collecting and assessing appropriate safety information at industry level, but also nationally and eu-wide – and making sure that safety initiatives are taken on the basis of that information – the european union will have the appropriate means to prevent further accidents. this text also brings significant improvements in the area of ‘just culture’ and this is an issue where parliament’s input has been crucial to achieving a good outcome. the text strongly reinforces protection for those who report occurrences and other aviation professionals. protecting the source of information should encourage more aviation professionals to report occurrences and other safety-related information.
