in writing. the union's objective of creating an area of freedom, security and justice should be achieved, in particular through the application of common measures forming an asylum and immigration policy, based on solidarity between member states, which is fair towards third countries and their nationals. the european council of 2[nbsp ]december[nbsp ]2009 noted that financial resources within the union should be able to be used in an increasingly flexible and coherent manner, both in terms of scope and applicability, to allow asylum and migration policy to evolve.
in writing. we welcome the council decision authorising member states to ratify or accede to the hong kong convention. this convention constitutes a first step at global level towards safer and more environmentally sound recycling of ships flying the flag of a third country, while emphasising that truly safe and environmentally sound recycling can only be achieved by going beyond the provisions of this convention, as the new eu regulation on ship recycling does.
in writing. the so-called 'troika' of the commission, the european central bank (ecb) and the international monetary fund (imf) has already intervened in four eu countries: greece, portugal, ireland and cyprus. although its intervention has probably helped these countries to avoid a short-term default, which is welcome, this report makes a severe assessment of its internal workings. this fact highlights the unequal distribution of responsibilities between the three institutions, the too wide differences in the way negotiations are conducted and the too many democratic shortcomings. the report also makes recommendations: implementation of clear, transparent and binding rules on interaction between the institutions of the troika; the creation of emergency channels in case the initial recommendations of the troika prove to be inaccurate or inappropriate; the aim of the project is to improve the understanding of social issues, improve communication and improve national support for the proposed plan. these measures are essential and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the crisis has shown that the existing framework for the economic governance of the union was not geared to combating this crisis. under considerable time pressure, rescue mechanisms and the troika were set up to help countries facing the greatest difficulties, to prevent disorderly insolvency and spillover of the crisis to other member states, and to prevent the breakdown of the euro area. the role of the ecb and the way decisions were taken in the troika were sometimes difficult to understand in these contexts. in future, therefore, it is all the more important that not only relations within the troika's organs are clear, transparent and governed by binding rules, but that tasks and responsibilities are also clearly defined. since the temporary european financial stability facility (efsf) and the permanent european stability mechanism (esm) were also established on an ad hoc basis as intergovernmental mechanisms, it is all the more important that the esm is integrated into the eu legal framework in the long term and is made accountable to the european parliament and the european council including for decisions on granting financial assistance .
in writing. the s&d group deplores the authoritarian and austerity policies of the troika and considers that it operates outside the legal framework of the union. we believe that technocrats cannot continue to give orders to the elected representatives of the people. europe needs a genuine european monetary fund, backed by eu law, to support countries in difficulty and to involve the european parliament in the decision-making process. the report concludes that the decisions of the troika are inappropriate and undemocratic and that it should be abolished. it recommended that the european commission set up a european monetary fund governed by eu law and a european stability mechanism. the international monetary fund would be an optional participant and the european central bank a tacit observer. in addition, country-specific solutions need to be implemented more rapidly, in addition to a medium-term reform at european level.
in writing. the unprecedented economic and financial crisis that has hit the european union since 2010 and the drastic measures taken to save greece, portugal, cyprus and ireland leave no one indifferent, as the impact on employment, health and the lives of the population in general is considerable. the first steps are now being taken, and the role of the troika, the body made up of representatives of the european central bank, the european commission and the international monetary fund, is being criticized. let us say it right away, the primary responsibility lies with the governments of these countries which have created this situation of bankruptcy, holding their people hostage for at least a decade! the responsibility of the eurogroup, which gave the troika a mandate, is also assumed. the intervention was necessary but the results showed its ineffectiveness: increasing debt, explosion of precariousness and a significant decrease in tax revenues. this is the conclusion of the cercas report on the social aspects of the troika's role, adopted this afternoon by a large majority of 408 votes, with a clearly stated aim: to turn the page and introduce crisis management mechanisms which will enable all the union's institutions to achieve social objectives.
in writing. in recent years, the social dimension of the union has been totally ignored. now europe must show that it is concerned not only about the financial health of the member states but also about the daily lives of its citizens. europe is not just a club of lenders, it is a community of values. this report focuses on the countries (greece, ireland, portugal and cyprus) which have been affected by the troika's economic adjustment programmes. it provides a thorough analysis of the social impact of these programmes. the report calls on the troika and the member states to end these programmes as soon as possible and to create a transparent crisis management mechanism within the eu institutions. it called on the commission to study, together with the international labour organisation (ilo) and the council of europe, the employment and social consequences of these adjustment programmes, with a view to proposing corrective measures and incentives to improve the situation of these countries in these areas.
in writing. the european union's internal affairs policy is to create an area of freedom, security and justice: an area without internal borders, where people can enter, move and live freely, with the certainty that their rights will be fully respected and their security guaranteed, in the light of common challenges, such as the development of a comprehensive union immigration policy to strengthen the union's competitiveness and social cohesion. this policy also includes the creation of a common european asylum system, the prevention of the threats posed by large-scale organised crime, and the fight against illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings, cybercrime and terrorism.
in writing. crime, and in particular organised crime, is a serious threat to the security of european citizens and to the development of the internal market. police cooperation between member states and with third countries is therefore an essential instrument for the effective fight against criminal phenomena which are now essentially transnational in nature. the fight against the networks typical of organised crime, including the recycling of illicit profits, meets the requirements of protecting the lawful economy and the market against possible distortions. the instrument for financial support for police cooperation, the prevention and repression of crime and crisis management constitutes, together with the asylum and migration instrument, one of the two pillars of the internal security fund provided for in the multiannual financial framework of the european union for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. the current practice of fixing, at the beginning of the mff, the annual allocations that member states will receive for the whole seven-year period is a guarantee of continuity and predictability (adequate programming). however, it is essentially a static method that does not provide incentives for member states to take action in response to the union's priorities and does not allow the union to react to changing situations and priorities. the allocation and implementation mechanism of the resources selected under the future home affairs funds should reconcile the need for continuity and stability with the need for flexibility and adaptation to change.
in writing. i support the overall objective of the proposed directive, namely to ensure a high common level of network and information security (nis). in order to improve the effectiveness of the proposed measures, your rapporteur considers that this directive, as a starting point, should be limited to certain operators, protect investments in network and information security that have already been made, and avoid duplication of institutional structures and obligations imposed on market players. i also believe that the directive in question should support the establishment of trusting relationships and the development of exchanges between public and private actors, and that the negative reactions manifested in the form of a mere 'culture of compliance' should be avoided in favour of the expected 'culture of risk management'. in view of these considerations, your rapporteur proposes to increase the impact of the directive by introducing a series of amendments.
in writing. with the financial market crisis since 2008, financial reporting and auditing have become a top priority of eu policy. an effective common framework for financial reporting is essential for the proper functioning of the internal market and capital markets and for the achievement of an integrated market for financial services in the union. in the light of the findings of 22 february 2013 of the uk competition commission on the market for the statutory audit of ftse 350 companies, controllers in particular should ensure that they are strictly independent of issuers in order to facilitate the efficient functioning of the union capital markets and to serve the shareholders, not the issuer's management.

in writing. the objective of this report is to assess the implementation of the lisbon treaty, paying particular attention to the impact of the main changes it has introduced on the interinstitutional relations between the european parliament and the commission since its entry into force. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and corruption, and to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented. in reality, even if the treaty of lisbon did not call into question the commission's role as the driving force behind european activity, the result is that over the last four years the commission has lost some of its political influence within the institutional architecture of the union. this erosion of the commission's powers is to a large extent linked to the economic and financial crisis, which is working rather in favour of the intervention and authority of the european council and, therefore, the progression of intergovernmental action to the detriment of the community method.
in writing. the sustainability of land governance depends on institutional reforms and capacity building programmes that must accompany the registration of land ownership and small businesses. public authorities have an important role to play in defining property rights and enforcing them through the courts and the police. however, contrary to widespread prejudice, the state is not the source or distributor of property, but its protector. normally charged with protecting legitimate land claims, national land titling systems have often been used to legalize land theft. the establishment of land reform and property rights requires a high degree of flexibility to allow for adaptation to local cultural and social conditions.

in writing. the arrest of mr sergei magnitsky and his death in prison in november 2009 is a flagrant and shocking case of disregard for fundamental rights in russia. these events bring back bad memories of the many violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms committed in that country. i strongly support the request to the council to take measures to ban visas to the european union and freeze the assets of 32 russian officials suspected of being responsible for the torture and death of russian lawyer sergei magnitsky and the 'repeated' harassment of his family members. the adoption of this text is part of the overall approach to remind russia of the respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law, which are the pillars and the very essence of the council of europe of which it is a member. i naturally support any initiative to fight impunity for human rights violations and by voting for this text i join parliament's call on russia to clarify the circumstances of mr magnitsky's death, bring the perpetrators to justice and put an end to the persecution against his family.

in writing. i believe that the follow-up and implementation of the declaration adopted at the high level meeting on the rule of law of 24 september 2012 should be actively promoted at national and international level, and that the extent to which the rule of law can be linked to the current reflection on the post-2015 mdgs should be explored. on the other hand, there is a need to strengthen international efforts to ensure that all human rights recognised by un conventions are considered to be universal, indivisible, interdependent and closely linked and are respected, and to promote the integration of human rights and fundamental freedoms into all aspects of the work of the un.
in writing. independent european broadcasters offer audiences in europe and around the world a common vision and defend the values enshrined in the eu treaties. furthermore, as the main source of information for citizens, broadcasting makes it possible to reach audiences in europe and in third countries efficiently and cost-effectively. it is therefore necessary to take account of the many opportunities offered by these media and to consider these tools as a vehicle that can play an essential role on the international scene and convey european values throughout the world. in this respect, it is essential to put in place a coherent strategy for the radio and television broadcasting of european media. the creation of a european radio service broadcasting throughout the world would be very useful not only in terms of the impact of european action but also as an overall instrument of the union's external relations.
in writing. the council must understand that free european media, and in particular a financially viable and independent public service broadcasting, are important for promoting democratic values and informing the public about the measures taken and the objectives pursued in the framework of the cfsp, in particular by fostering a better understanding of the issues that unite and divide europe and a more uniform understanding of foreign policy among european citizens. a coherent and robust strategy on european media broadcasting in the union's external relations should be established, thereby promoting freedom of expression and media pluralism while protecting and strengthening democracy and human rights in europe and in third countries, and made an integral tool of the cfsp.
in writing. we consider it also important to protect blind people and vulnerable users by installing an appropriate warning system on electric vehicles. parliament and the council have agreed on the mandatory nature of such a system; it was agreed that this provision will be applicable within 3 years of the implementation of the regulation for all new vehicles and within 5 years for all electric-hybrid and electric vehicles. we also attach great importance to the problems of road pavement and its role in reducing vehicle noise. parliament and the council agreed that the commission should develop guidelines for information and good practice on the technological development of coating and its classification, on the basis of information provided by the member states. a recital to that effect has been inserted in the regulation.
in writing. we support the amendment of the provisions on databases proposed by the commission. as a direct consequence of the amendment of regulation (ec) no[nbsp ]1760/2000, this revision is necessary and appropriate. however, beyond the commission's proposal, we suggest adding 'the means of identification used' to the information requested from operators about their operations. this is to ensure accurate and up-to-date knowledge of the level of use of the two means available for the identification of bovine animals.
in writing. the european union currently has no horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. the proposed instrument is legitimately designed to strengthen the enforcement of the union's trade rights, to establish its credibility and, ultimately, to convince our trading partners to respect the rules of the game laid down in trade agreements. the proposal is also part of a strategy to broaden the union's markets and align the decision-making process with the lisbon treaty. the aim of this text is therefore to provide the union with an appropriate instrument to ensure the effective exercise of its rights under international trade agreements, in order to safeguard its economic interests. it is therefore very important that the union should adopt this horizontal instrument as soon as possible in order to be able to enforce its rights when a trading partner does not respect its commitments.
in writing. the european union currently has no horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. in a world where retaliation is on the rise, the proposed instrument is legitimately designed to strengthen the enforcement of the union's trade rights, to establish its credibility and, ultimately, to convince our trading partners to respect the rules of the game laid down in trade agreements. the proposal under consideration is also part of a strategy to widen the union's markets and aligns the decision-making process with the lisbon treaty. this new instrument should also be considered within the framework of multilateral (wto), regional and bilateral dispute settlement rules and procedures, which already give the complainant country the right to choose the 'last resort' option, under which it can temporarily take defensive retaliatory measures against the offending country when it refuses to comply with a decision of a dispute settlement body. this instrument is therefore not intended to be protectionist in any way.
in writing. i am not opposed to bangladesh being charged an export tax. however, this decision should be taken by the legislators in bangladesh and not by the european institutions. we asked the commission why it included such references and provisions in its proposal, but it did not give a satisfactory answer. i am therefore satisfied that the rapporteur has deleted these references and provisions from the regulation and has introduced a new recital which recognises bangladesh's right to levy an export tax of an amount which he deems appropriate. it is essential to stress that the regulation must be in line with the general provisions of article 208 tfeu and the general objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions in bangladesh and poverty eradication in bangladesh. the rapporteur has therefore introduced a new recital and a new paragraph in article 1 of the regulation.
in writing. medical devices are instruments, software or implants used for diagnosis, monitoring, treatment or replacement in the event of injury or disability. there is a wide range of these, from low-risk products such as corrective lenses, adhesive plasters, etc., to high-risk devices such as cardiac regulators and hip replacements. since the regulatory framework currently governing medical devices dates from 1990 and 1993, it requires substantial updating to keep pace with technological and scientific progress on the one hand and to harmonise its implementation on the other. recent scandals, such as breast implant fraud and problems with metal prostheses of the coxofemoral joint, have shown that the authorisation system in place is not suitable for high-risk devices. under the current system, notified bodies assess the performance and safety of medical devices. however, this process and the remuneration demanded from producers are not sufficiently transparent.
in writing. there is a consensus that the european union should not seek to restrict access to dna testing for patients but that appropriate genetic counselling should be systematically offered to inform them of the consequences before the test is carried out. in order to respect the principle of subsidiarity, it should be for the member states to regulate the modalities and member states should have the possibility to go beyond what is required by the regulation. it could even be argued that it is mandatory to include informed consent in the proposal because it is a crucial element of the charter of fundamental rights (article 3) and the charter of fundamental rights is legally binding on the european union in the areas where it intervenes.
in writing. we can be satisfied with the commission's proposal and i believe that the new accounts will help to develop new, more comprehensive indicators to improve public debate and policy-making. in view of the financial and staff constraints currently facing the national statistical institutes, it is important to focus on improving the quality and encouraging the use of existing modules and those which the commission has put forward in the proposal under consideration. the additional administrative burden should be kept to a minimum. after consulting various data collection services, it became clear that some member states were not yet ready for this new exercise and wanted to postpone its implementation by one year. i can support the idea of a deferral, as long as it benefits the quality of the data provided by the member states to eurostat. the widespread use of environmental accounting data by the european commission and national administrations can only be encouraged, with the aim of developing targeted policies that can contribute to the union's policy priorities of green growth and resource efficiency.
in writing. this text is part of a broad movement to raise awareness among european public opinion of the european union's external action in developing countries. a broad public support and strong political support are essential to the success of the union's development action. i am well aware that european development policy is currently suffering from a lack of public image. i support any initiative to remedy this image deficit. the european year for development (2015) should therefore serve as a catalyst to raise public awareness through public policy debate, and to provide impetus and enable the exchange of good practice between member states, local and regional authorities, civil society, including local associations in developing countries, local partners, trade unions and entities and organisations. the year 2015 will be a good opportunity to recall that the right to respect for human dignity is not dependent on a person's place of residence or heritage, but that the irreducibility of human dignity is the basic principle of all european policy.
in writing. the legislative initiative which is the subject of this report is the result of a public awareness campaign involving representatives of the economic and social committee, the committee of the regions, concord and the european parliament. a dedicated round table at the 2012 european development days provided an opportunity to spread the idea to a wider audience. the commission also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in the european union. the proposed legislation is therefore the culmination of a major awareness-raising effort.
in writing. the proposed programme aims to contribute to the creation of an independent european space surveillance and tracking capability for orbiting objects (sst) to prevent and monitor the increasing risk of collision between space infrastructure and other space vehicles or debris. the need for osh is shared at international and national levels by both governments and industry in general, which are dependent on space infrastructure. it is also important to ensure the long-term availability of european space assets, such as the satellites of the galileo and copernicus programmes. this is the first attempt of its kind at union level and the commission proposes to start by pooling the resources and skills available in the member states and providing services to users. we propose that the esa know-how be taken into account in an agreement between esa and the participating member states. esa is the only body with competence at european level for osh and more generally for ash. if esa cannot manage or control the programme, it should be able to contribute to it.
in writing. in the current financial framework, food security budget lines were under the same heading as the common agricultural policy (cap), but the new structure of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework provides for the shift of food security budget lines from heading two to heading three. this transfer of appropriations for the 2014-2020 programming period entails a significant risk of budget shortfall in the event of a very large-scale animal disease outbreak. if such an outbreak should occur, the union must be able to mobilise, very quickly, additional funds to finance emergency veterinary or phytosanitary measures and thus prevent further losses. in this context, the commission proposal provides for access to the agricultural crisis reserve to respond to emergency situations in the veterinary or phytosanitary sector. however, a solution is needed to strengthen the food security budget, if necessary, should such large-scale agricultural crises occur. unfortunately, given the limited overall allocation for the eu budget for 2014-2020, identifying a fund that could be used in these cases is not easy.
in writing. council regulation (ec) no[nbsp]2173/2005 establishes a licensing regime for 'forest law enforcement, governance and trade', known as flegt (forest law enforcement, government and trade). this scheme was set up to combat the problem of illegal logging and the associated trade. it applies to specified wood and derived products exported from 'partner countries', i.e. countries which have voluntary partnership agreements with the european union. it thus ensures that only timber and derived products legally harvested in accordance with the national legislation of these partner countries may enter the union. the import of certain timber and derived products from the partner countries without a flegt import authorisation is prohibited. six states are currently implementing this system under a voluntary partnership agreement (cameroon, ghana, indonesia, liberia, the central african republic and the republic of congo); six other countries are in negotiations with the union to conclude such agreements.
in writing. making clinical trials of medicines for human use more transparent, clearer and more uniform is a vital necessity for the proper functioning of the health system at european level. this transparency, clarity and uniformity of the rules in this area will improve the protection of patients and their access to appropriate treatment. indeed, the coordination and coherent application of policies at local level is one of the major challenges facing the european union. i encourage efforts to harmonize and coordinate policies at union level. in addition, working at european level in the field of health will reduce the cost and burden of conducting transnational clinical trials. i look forward to the scientific advances that the proposal will bring.
in writing. the general consensus among stakeholders is that the current legislation on clinical trials needs to be revised as a matter of urgency. the number of clinical trials conducted in europe has declined sharply in recent years, at least in part due to some of the measures introduced by the clinical trials directive. between 2007 and 2011, the number of clinical trials conducted in the european union fell by 25%, and many trials are now being conducted in emerging economies. this decline not only has serious economic consequences but also hinders medical advances, to the detriment of patients. europe must be competitive and attractive to pharmaceutical companies wishing to carry out research, but at the same time it must promote academic research and encourage the development of medicines to treat rare diseases. at the same time, europe should be a world reference in patient safety and transparency, in order to gain public trust and promote the quality of science.
in writing. three years after the fukushima nuclear disaster (march 2011), it is important to take the management of the nuclear issue seriously. i support the approach of my colleagues in parliament to harmonize and make the nuclear safety directive's management framework effective and preventive. i strongly recommend that member states take the lessons of the fukushima accident into account and i call on them to fulfil their obligations with regard to the establishment and maintenance of a national framework for nuclear safety. after the fukushima accident, a number of requirements were established by the european council. states must take seriously the respect of these obligations, in particular the peer review of the safety of power stations every six years, in the context of stress tests.
in writing. following the fukushima accident, the commission and the european nuclear safety regulators group (ensreg) carried out stress tests which resulted in a series of recommendations and a suggestion to amend the nuclear safety directive. this proposal aims to amend, strengthen and supplement that directive by combining technical improvements and broader security considerations such as governance, transparency and preparedness and responsiveness on site. the s&d group (and the report) supported the provisions on periodic self-evaluations and peer reviews, six-monthly peer reviews of given areas, and the provision that the area of this first six-monthly evaluation will be decided within three years of the entry into force of the directive.
in writing. ensuring tax equity across all income groups is not only a moral imperative; it is also the most economically sound way to ensure that taxes are collected and used to their fullest potential. without creating new taxation, this additional revenue for member states would allow for new investment in job creation, growth-enhancing programmes and infrastructure. at a time when europe is still reeling from the consequences of the crisis, we cannot afford to remain idle. in the context of the union's continuing efforts to close the existing tax loopholes arising from the exploitation of differences between member states' tax systems, double non-taxation, as well as extreme forms of under-taxation, deprive member states of significant revenues and foster conditions of unfair competition between undertakings operating within the single market. in the interests of fairness and transparency, as well as competition and economic efficiency, the union must do its utmost to rectify its fiscal shortfall rapidly.
in writing. the stockholm programme aims to strengthen the area of justice, freedom and security through actions that focus on the interests and needs of citizens. the mid-term review of this programme should provide a basis for addressing future challenges in the area of justice, freedom and security. despite the progress made since the launch of this programme in 2010, the implementation of certain chapters should be strengthened. i am, for example, in favour of strengthening the promotion of citizens. moreover, greater attention should be paid to the special situation of vulnerable groups such as the roma. i would also like to reiterate my concern about the mass surveillance of eu citizens. finally, i would like to welcome the union's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. this should ensure an additional level of protection for citizens and persons for whom the union is responsible, in particular in the context of the area of freedom, security and justice. i therefore urge all the parties concerned to ratify the convention as soon as possible.
in writing. the stockholm programme is a multiannual strategy (2009-2014) aimed at building a europe of freedom, security and justice. the european council adopted the stockholm programme in 2009, calling for a mid-term evaluation in 2012. the main point was to ensure the follow-up of this programme and the fact that it was no longer to be drawn up solely by the council but, in the spirit of the lisbon treaty, in the framework of a joint exercise by the european parliament, the commission and the council. other key points included the assessment of criminal justice using a scoreboard and a reference to the copenhagen criteria which called for both candidate and current member states to respect common values. the s&d group has collected more than 77 signatures, together with the alliance of liberals and democrats (alde) and the greens, for an amendment on the need to regularly assess member states' compliance with the eu's fundamental values. the group intends to remain firm on this issue and not to allow the important achievements or references of the current legislature to be undermined.
in writing. the updating of the annexes to regulation (ec) no 428/2009 on dual-use goods, which include the lists of controlled goods and destinations, is currently under way in the ordinary legislative procedure. this proposal for post-lisbon alignment aims to streamline the procedures applied under the european export control system by introducing delegated acts for the regular updating of annex i and the consequent amendment of annex ii. following the adoption of parliament's first reading position on 23 october 2012, informal negotiations to reach an agreement at an early second reading were concluded on 17 december 2013. the text of the negotiations was approved by a very large majority in the international trade committee on 21 january 2014. after linguistic verification, the council adopted its position at first reading on 3[nbsp ]march[nbsp ]2014, confirming the agreement.
in writing. the aviation sector is highly international. i argue that a comprehensive approach to the problem of emissions from international aviation is the best way to ensure long-term sustainability. this is part of our efforts to achieve a future international agreement to control greenhouse gas emissions from aviation. at european level, it is already up to the member states to decide what to do with the proceeds of the auctioning of allowances. the objective is to use these revenues to combat climate change in the union and in third countries and to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. we want to extend this system to aviation in order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from this sector and thus contribute to the global fight against climate change.
in writing. the suspensive legislation on international aviation emissions (iaea) was a temporary derogation from the provisions of the directive on emission trading standards 2003/87/ec. this derogation was intended to facilitate international progress towards the adoption of a global market-based measure. the new commission proposal takes an airspace approach: it will apply from 2014, but only covers a certain proportion of emissions (no more than 12nm outside the european economic area) from flights arriving in and departing from non-eu countries. at the same time, the suspensive legislation remains in force for an additional year. in addition, flights within the european economic area are fully covered by the directive.

in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on payment services in the internal market, amending directives 2002/65/ec, 2013/36/eu and 2009/110/ec and repealing directive 2007/64/ec and share the choices of compromise amendments voted
in writing. new communication technologies are an essential tool for everyday life in the 21st century, whether in private or in the workplace. it is "a component of the public space where new forms of cross-border trade are emerging and opportunities for european businesses in the global digital economy are being created, alongside the development of an innovative market and socio-cultural exchanges". effective regulation of the single market for electronic communications would avoid the disruption that could result from a possible lax approach in this important area. by voting for this text, i support the protection of net neutrality which will support the global single telecoms market and is essential to create a safe environment for investment in this sector and thus allow for competitiveness, growth and job creation.
in writing. the european parliament voted today for the digital single market. the new european digital market should bring in 400 euros per person per year. it is highly employment-generating, will give consumers more information and security and will lower telephone charges by eliminating roaming charges. finally, the guarantee of a genuine net neutrality was obtained by a few votes. this is very good news for the european citizen. the amendments we have asked for and obtained have achieved this result, although this was very much disputed and the gap between the epp and other conservatives and the rest of parliament was once again immense.
in writing. today, electronic transactions are booming like never before. the establishment of a mechanism to harmonise electronic identification, signature and authentication in a uniform manner across the union seems to me to be essential to guarantee the security and safety of electronic transactions. this system would be based on a mutual recognition mechanism between member states. by supporting this resolution and the institutional trilogue agreement of february 2014, i am joining the overall approach to regulate and harmonise the functioning of the electronic market, which is increasingly following the conventional market. it is important to act without delay to prevent the negative effects that can arise from the existence of a multitude of systems such as fraud and cybercrime.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. the european union does not have a comprehensive transnational and cross-sectoral framework for making electronic transactions secure, reliable and easy, covering electronic identification, authentication and trust services. the relevant union legislation in force, namely directive 1999/93/ec on a community framework for electronic signatures, as its name indicates, concerns only electronic signatures. the digital strategy for europe identifies the current obstacles to europe's digital development and proposes legislation on trust services and mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication, establishing a clear legal framework to address the bottlenecks and lack of interoperability, develop digital citizenship and prevent cybercrime. legislation ensuring the mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication within the union is also a key action in the single market act and the roadmap for stability and growth. the european parliament has repeatedly stressed the importance of the security of electronic services.

in writing. it is time for parliament to speak out in favour of promoting a more coherent eu foreign policy, whether in institutional, financial or partnership terms with other countries and regional organisations. one of the major challenges facing the union is the effective coordination of its policies and their implementation at local level. i encourage greater cooperation between the commission and the european external action service (eeas). this cooperation should be achieved through the organisation of regular and institutionalised meetings between the commissioners responsible for external relations and other commissioners with competence in the different foreign affairs policies, such as development, trade, energy, environment, internal market and migration. i support the establishment of a comprehensive approach that would define an efficient response to multidimensional crises and promote human security worldwide.
in writing. significant geostrategic changes are also underway in other parts of the world, including the emergence of a multipolar international scene characterised by the presence of new actors with competing regional and global ambitions, and increasing interdependence. the rise of multidimensional and asymmetric threats; the reorientation of us security policy towards the asia-pacific region; the growing struggle for energy and resource security; the increasingly serious consequences of climate change; and a severe and protracted global economic and financial crisis from which no member state of the european union is immune. i would like to stress that in such a geopolitical climate, the european union must preserve and promote its values, interests and stability on the world stage, while protecting the security and prosperity of its citizens. this situation requires a new approach to shaping, in collaboration with our strategic partners, a new multipolar world order that is inclusive, credible, just, cooperative, based on respect for human rights, the rule of law and democracy, and aimed at achieving the settlement of disputes without resorting to armed conflict.

the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to thank you for your reply. first of all, in the absence of our rapporteur, mr carlo fidanza, i would like to thank his colleagues who have contributed to this dossier. we also want to thank the staff of the commission and the council for reaching agreement at first reading. of course, as so often, the council was not very ambitious in this outcome, but we can live with the result. it is almost symptomatic to talk about alternative fuels at the end of the legislative period, because it was one of the cornerstones when we said at the beginning of this period with the white paper, among other things, that in transport these alternative fuels are one of the challenges, that we are of course not only supporting an alternative, but also an energy mix. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. minimum requirements for the construction of the infrastructure are provided. the countries must prepare a national policy framework and submit it here no later than 24 months after the publication of this directive. cross-border coverage should also be announced. it is well known that the specific features of alternative fuels, on the one hand, and the information provided to citizens, on the other, have led to the fact that very few people today are turning to these alternatives for fear of not having the infrastructure in border areas tomorrow and of having problems as a result. technical neutrality was also an important point for us. so we went in a two-phase rhythm. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy policy and its implementation in the member states. this is one of the reasons why the proposal here is that there should be a charging station for ten electric vehicles. the fact that the core network at the charging stations is also to be provided for and that this will have to be particularly reviewed from 2025 onwards is self-evident, because this also leads to the priorities of the trans-european networks as a whole. as far as liquefied natural gas is concerned, we are also proposing a two-stage approach. the commission will also assess the impact of the measures on the environment and the environment protection of natural resources. we know that this is of course also associated with certain costs and that a realistic approach should be taken accordingly. but we also know the other challenge, especially in this area, that there is a really high expectation of alternative fuels. we therefore think it is very good that we are making the transeuropean networks a binding priority in the existing core network and also in the work here tomorrow. in conclusion, i would like to remind you that this proposal not only addresses the issue of dependence on oil for up to 90% of transport, but also the issue of europe's energy dependence - 84% of which is imported - but also suggests concrete alternatives. the third important point is the reduction of the environmental impact of transport and the corresponding improvement in the quality of life in urban areas, where it is proved that up to 80% of people will live in the next ten or fifteen years. and last but not least, we must not forget that in this area too we must secure europe's position as the research and development site, and that every action and decision in this area also strengthens the technology we support and the european site. in that sense we can agree with the result. as i said at the beginning, it is not as ambitious as we had hoped, but we can consider it a good result.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, honourable members, thank you very much for your observations. it is important that you vote tomorrow in favour of this proposal. the directive on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure will have a decisive impact on how we see transport. new technologies will open up new horizons and opportunities for the european automotive and transport industry within europe and on the global market. it is vitally important for the good health of our economy. of course, our work does not stop here. it has only just started. the commission will closely monitor how member states implement this directive. if appropriate, we will progress to an action plan on its implementation and review. of course, i must also say that this directive cannot cover all issues. we have other documents and other decisions; for instance, how to promote sustainable urban mobility, and we even have an abbreviation: sumps – sustainable urban mobility plans. we promote it and encourage member states to develop public transport and sustainable urban mobility. however, this directive cannot cover all issues; it is about clean power in transport. the commission would like to thank the outgoing parliament for all its work and contribution in making transport cleaner, more efficient and less dependent on oil.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, the proposal being debated today has multiple benefits. it encourages the use of low-carbon propulsion technologies and makes trucks more aerodynamic. it is good for vulnerable road users, because a different cabin design will improve drivers’ vision. it will also help european lorry manufacturers to sell the truck of the future in the global market. it will make road transport greener and safer. the commission would like to thank the rapporteur, mr leichtfried, and the shadow rapporteurs for the progress they have made. many of the amendments voted by committee clarify or strengthen the proposal. the commission welcomes these amendments. the commission takes note of the compromise reached on the cross-border traffic of longer vehicles. there are a number of amendments where the commission has concerns. the first i want to mention is the 50 cm limit imposed for rear devices. this is already allowed today, under the type-approval legislation. however, aerodynamic performance improves continuously up to two metres. keeping the 50 cm limit means forgoing important benefits in terms of lower emissions and fuel consumption. another amendment makes new cabin designs mandatory seven years after the directive has entered into force. this is contrary to the current approach, which is to promote more aerodynamic vehicles without mandating a specific design. the commission also has reservations regarding the use of the term ‘combined transport’ instead of ‘intermodal transport’. it only applies to transport between eu member states, whereas 45-foot containers are increasingly used in ocean-going transport. in addition, on-board weighing systems should not be made mandatory. member states which have invested in infrastructure for weighing moving vehicles should be allowed to continue this method. all in all, the commission appreciates the progress made on most of the amendments. this forms a very good basis for advancing the file under the new parliament. i look forward to the debate.

working since the first minute, and others who have been working until the last, and we are among them. i would like to thank all the colleagues who have helped to make the best of this dossier. we have not been and still are not in agreement. we've signed compromises to make the whole dossier move forward. we must not forget that the purpose of weights and measures was primarily to improve safety and also to improve aerodynamics, and thus to have a partial positive impact on consumers and the environment. the fact that the whole subject was then, of course, very much about this crossborder transport for larger lorries is perhaps understandable in view of the proximity of certain elections, including the european elections. but it would have been a pity if we had missed any good developments in this area. so i see the result at this point with a laughing eye where we have found good compromises for the technology, and with a tearful eye where we have not found them. because i think that if a truck has to cross a border with almost nothing to make a four tonne difference, that's not the best sign for the environment either. the commission has already completed part of the task it has now been given: this study on larger lorries. she had the same problem as many of her colleagues, that she did not agree with the results of the study. but you can't keep doing studies until you like the results. so we're hoping that the next result of the study will be maybe a little bit more what you've been expecting. but we must not question the study as such, because i think one thing is clear: we will not make the railway more efficient by slowing down the road. i also believe that what we are proposing here is not a breakdown of the railway, but an improvement in the efficiency of the road. we will not agree on that in future either, that is part of the debate. i am grateful for the frank debate we have had - even with differences of opinion - and for the compromises we have found.
on behalf of the s&d group, i agree with what my colleague and rapporteur, jörg leichtfried, has said about the role of parliament. i would remind you that the commission first tried, somewhat "in a hurry", to allow the crossborder transport of megatransporters by means of a reinterpretation of the existing rules. we have been very insistent that this should be regulated by legislation and that legislation should be brought to light in a timely manner and with the knowledge of the facts. my group - and this is no secret - is not in favour of extending the use of megatrucks. we believe that this is contrary to the objectives which the european commission itself has set out in its white paper on transport, namely to promote long-distance transport mainly by means of sustainable modes of transport such as rail and inland waterway. we are prepared to debate this and we will look at the impact assessments that follow with the necessary attention and then we as a parliament will have to cut the knots. the proposal to adapt the weights and measures to new technological developments is of course positive, so that lorries consume less fuel, emit less co2 and are safer, protect vulnerable road users better and increase driver comfort. this section, mr rapporteur, and the shadow rapporteurs who have worked on it, is clearly a step forward and should encourage the sector to finally bring a more aerodynamic model to the market and perhaps thereby to take over markets outside europe as well. on the whole, we have a good proposal here and we as a group will support it fully. "blue card" is the answer. thank you for asking. i am not a big fan of this pilot project myself, but we have accepted that it will take place. it's good to evaluate the project thoroughly. but in fact it is a status quo with respect to the current european rules. you know that pilot projects can, should and will continue to be possible. that does not change, but we do not want to encourage it across borders. so let us do that pilot project in flanders, let us evaluate it and let us, in the meantime, have a better debate at european level and then, with impact studies and so on, see what the overall effect is on the transport system and on other matters such as infrastructure costs, road safety and so on. that should be our main concern.

i would prefer to concentrate on the 'official controls' aspect. it is essential that controls be carried out independently and that the final control be carried out by the public authorities. self-control is a good thing, it may be encouraged in the sector, but it is the government's final task to provide a stick behind the door. let us look back at the past. almost every food scandal has arisen where either the government was poorly organized, or where official controls were subject to a logic of greed and profit at all costs, or where commercial interests were considered more important than the interests of public health. strong and independent government oversight is crucial. the role of the official veterinarian is also crucial in the meat sector. checks, if any, by technicians shall be carried out under his or her authority. finally, i regret that the commission's good proposal, which gave member states the possibility of calling out the wrongdoer, has been watered down. i think this is the only flaw in the excellent report drawn up under the leadership of mr perelló rodríguez. thank you for that.

this is a particularly timely debate, because we all know how important smes are to our economy. and if you talk to a lot of business leaders or people who want to start, there are a few things that come up all the time. we can send some of these things from the european parliament. we shall have to delegate other matters to the member states. one of the most important things is to provide adequate training, not only for people who want to start their own businesses, but also for people who need to be employed by those smes. today we are faced in europe with a very high level of youth unemployment, and yet we see that there are still vacancies in various smes. so finding a better match on the labour market seems to me to be one of the priorities for europe and for our member states. secondly, there is everything to do with the regulations we are making here in the european parliament. we must sometimes consider the impact of these regulations on smes. the european commission is developing good initiatives to assess whether the impact of such regulations on small businesses is adequate or not and whether they need to be adjusted. the last point is all that has to do with financing. if companies are to grow, they must also be adequately financed, not only through banks but also through the capital markets. this will need to be addressed in the coming years to ensure that bank financing is restored and that other forms of financing are also made available to smes. my report on improving financing for smes is an attempt to do that.
for the greens/efa group madam president, "never again!" how many times have we heard those words? never again should the taxpayer be forced to bail out a failing bank. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's financial institutions are able to compete with the banks of other member states. the texts to be adopted today are undoubtedly a step forward in this respect. clearly, the owners, shareholders and creditors of the banks will be fined much sooner than the taxpayer. but i cannot help but be surprised that during these negotiations the member states, supported by the european central bank, supported by part of the european commission and in particular the services of mr rehn, who, according to the latest news, is a liberal, fought to insert into these texts a clause called preventive recapitalisation, which would allow the states to come to the rescue of their failing banks before they are really in a state of failure. in other words, to remedy the fact that the markets would no longer trust such a bank, by coming to its rescue. i am surprised at this attitude because it means that we will not recapitalise unless we do so soon enough. i think that's unacceptable. secondly, it is no longer possible for banks to be transnational when they live and become national again when they die. the text of the mrv also makes progress in this area, in the sense that we are moving towards greater federalisation of crisis management. but once again, the big banks will be managed [n] when in trouble by a consortium of states and not by the european commission. finally, mr barnier, my only regret about your action is that the main text, which was supposed to put an end to the existence of the banks deemed 'too big to fail', arrived too late, so that during this parliamentary term it could not be dealt with by this parliament. banks that are considered too big to fail should simply not exist! the text you have tabled goes in that direction and i regret that we have not been able to take it up this time.
who would have thought at the start of this parliamentary term that we would be putting the finishing touches to a real banking union, with a common supervisory and settlement mechanism and a uniform guarantee scheme for savers? we have done what we set out to do and we can be proud of our work. our sustained efforts, aimed at concrete results through the implementation of an ambitious but feasible building plan, have really helped europe to move forward. by working courageously together in this house, but also with the council and the european commission, and in particular with commissioner barnier and his team, we are achieving more than those who promised miracles or those who want to send europe into the desert as a scapegoat. we are proud of our success in opposing excessive national reflexes, in mechanisms that help to break vicious circles, in the nature of the banking union which is open to countries outside the euro zone and in the promotion of a secure financial system where, if it still fails, a bank can be wound up in one weekend according to legally secure and fair rules and without the savers and taxpayers having to bear the brunt of it. but of course, we are particularly proud of the fact that all these new rules also give us a new perspective that the banking sector can do what it should do, namely, to ensure that it plays a role in the real economy, so that we can get back to sustainable growth and create jobs in the private sector. i just want to thank everyone for their cooperation. it is by working together that we can achieve these results and it is also by working together in europe that we will be strong in the world.
in writing. we want to avoid the citizen having to pay the bill again. in the event of the bankruptcy of his european bank, he will be able to recover up to 100[nbsp ]000 euros of his savings within 7 days. on the other hand, it is not the citizen but the shareholders and creditors who will bear the first losses of their bank. with this text, as of 1 january 2016, it is first the shareholders and creditors who will assume the losses of their bank. we have improved the bank resolution process, which is the orderly restructuring and liquidation of a bank, in a preventive manner, when it is on the verge of bankruptcy. this will avoid the 'bankrise' as a 'systemic' impact on the rest of the economy. in the event of bankruptcy, the european citizen can recover up to €100,000 of his savings within 7 days. the deposit protection system is finally harmonized.
mr president, i would like to return to one aspect of this text, the famous 'made in'. we are well aware, and others have said it before me, that this is not a perfect tracing instrument as it appears in this text. it may not be the best place in a text on product safety to work on 'made in' either, but i remain firmly convinced that we must move forward on this subject and that it is extremely important. it is a valuable tool for relocating our economy and therefore, from a strictly ecological point of view, it is extremely important. it is also very important for consumers, to give them a means, a tool to make their consumer choice. and it is precisely because it is blocked in the council and because it is difficult that we must keep this 'made in' in the text and reject the amendment which seeks to remove it. it is a signal to the commission, to your successor, that we must move forward on this matter. it is also a signal, if we remember it, that we can also give to the council to make this 'made in' a real instrument for relocating and reviving the economy in europe. i think this is an opportunity and i hope that many of us will seize it.
in writing. the banking union became a reality this afternoon with the vote on three texts essential for the stability of the euro area: a single resolution mechanism in the event of bank failures, a framework for managing bank failures and a deposit guarantee scheme. measures that complement the single supervisory mechanism, adopted in september 2013, giving the european central bank (ecb) responsibility for supervising banks in the euro area. at present, 128 establishments are supervised. finally, the creation of a single fund is excellent news, a fund which banks have been able to raise to avoid having to resort to public money for their "rescue", as was sometimes done during the crisis. the depositors' savings will be even more protected, even beyond the legal protection threshold of eur 100000. the european union has shown its resolve in this long period of crisis: no, the euro zone has not collapsed! but the bailout of the banking sector came at a price: 26% of european gdp was absorbed by this task. banks now have to provide foreign exchange and facilitate access to credit and finance for individuals and entrepreneurs creating growth and jobs.

in writing. savers no longer have to contribute in the event of bank failure. that is the strong and fair message sent this afternoon by the european parliament with the adoption of the new directive on deposit guarantee schemes. the creation of a single fund is therefore excellent news: it will be enriched by the banks in order to avoid the need for public money. this will also increase the protection of depositors' savings, even if the legal protection threshold is eur 100 000. i would like to highlight some other real advances: the principle of contributions based on the risk profiles of the banking institution is enshrined; the repayment periods in the event of insolvency are increased from the current 20 working days to no later than seven working days in 2023; member states will also have to protect for a limited period of time (between 3 and 12 months) large amounts above the guarantee level of eur 100 000 arising in particular from the sale of private immovable property, insurance benefits, divorce. these are the "new rights" for savers, who must at the same time be able to benefit from easier access to bank loans. this is the next political battle to be fought!
in writing. the council's position at first reading is in line with the agreement reached in the trilogues, and we recommend that the committee adopt it without further amendments. deposit guarantee schemes, in addition to their primary function of protecting depositors, are also essential for the stability of the financial system, in particular in times of crisis. if customers lose confidence in their credit institution and at the same time attempt to withdraw their deposits, a phenomenon known as a bank run, this can not only lead to the collapse of an already unstable institution, but can also, due to a widespread loss of confidence, spread to other credit institutions and even to other states. no credit institution can hold the extremely high amount of liquidity required to guarantee deposits. the european commission therefore presented on 12[nbsp ]july[nbsp ]2010 a proposal for a revision of the deposit guarantee schemes directive. the commission considered that the completion of a common internal market required the remedying of excessive delays in the repayment of depositors' claims in the event of insolvency and of the significant differences in the financial resources of guarantee schemes between member states.

in writing. - i very much welcome this report, which provides for a common european framework for the resolution of banks and which significantly reduces the use of taxpayers' or depositors' money. in the context of the financial crisis, the situation of fragile or failing credit institutions has led member states to resort to taxpayers' money to rescue banks. this recourse is now minimised by a so-called priority of claims, by first involving the shareholders, then the bondholders of an institution and then the large depositors and, if this is not sufficient, by requiring the intervention of national resolution systems and resolution funds. the current state guarantee for all bank deposits up to eur 100 000 is being strengthened by requiring each country to set up its own deposit guarantee fund in order to be able to comply with the state guarantee. these new rules on banking union will provide additional protection for eu citizens' deposits, keep the cost to taxpayers as low as possible and, above all, prevent further destabilisation of financial markets.

in writing. ecall is activated automatically as soon as the on-board sensors detect a major accident. the system then dials the european emergency number 112, establishes a telephone link with the appropriate emergency call centre and transmits the details of the accident to the emergency services, including the time of the accident, the exact position of the vehicle involved and the direction taken by the vehicle. the ecall system shall be activated by the driver, the driver's assistant and the driver's representative. according to the commission, an ecall on 112 can reduce the time taken to respond to an emergency by 40% in urban areas and by 50% in rural areas
