the agenda calls for the debate on the recommendation for second reading of the committee on employment and social affairs on increasing worker mobility by improving the acquisition and preservation of supplementary pension rights (17612/1/2013 - c7-0059/2014 - 2005/0214 ((cod)) (rapporteur: ria oomen-ruijten) (a7-0188/2014).
on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, our position on the reports on the green and white papers on pensions is clear. the first pillar of the legal and public pension must be the foundation for a decent retirement. but it is equally clear that if the second pillar can provide a supplement to pensions, then it must benefit everyone fairly, including mobile workers between member states. but for years, as our rapporteur and our commissioner have pointed out, we have had an unfair situation in which these mobile workers could lose the benefit of their pension contributions in the context of supplementary pensions. some blocked the adoption of the directive to preserve their occupational pension model, while regularly selling us the benefits of worker mobility... thanks to the efforts of parliament, the negotiating team and above all the role played by ria oomen-ruijten and pervenche berès, both of whom i thank in particular, this is now settled. the mobile worker in the union will retain his rights. national models of supplementary pension had to be preserved with sufficient but not too long waiting and acquisition periods, which would have been a brake on mobility. of course, efforts have had to be made to preserve national models of supplementary pensions with sufficiently long waiting and acquisition periods for the systems to be financially viable. the balance struck seems to me to be good, with the combined waiting period and acquisition period not exceeding three years. in addition, thanks to the efforts of the parliament, there is no longer any question of requiring the mobile worker to find a new job in both member states immediately after he has settled in a new member state in order to benefit from the protection of his rights in the old one. this idea of the council was deeply unfair to all the workers who moved, for example, first for family reasons and then had to look for work in their new state. finally, we have managed to avoid the possibility for the managers of the second pillar to repay in cash what they consider to be 'small accounts'. this could only be done with the consent of the beneficiary, who would be duly informed of the consequences for his pension. that's an important part of it. in short, parliament and its negotiating team have brought social justice into the council and commission's common desire to promote worker mobility.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place today at 6 p.m. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda calls for the report by danuta jazlowiecka, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council implementing directive 96/71/ec on the posting of workers in the framework of the provision of services (com (((2012) 0131 c70086/2012 2012/0061 ((cod)) (a70249/2013).
mr president, commissioner, social dumping seriously harms the economic health of europe and the diversion of the application of the directive on the posting of workers is the best proof of this. for belgium alone [nbsp ]my country[nbsp ], in 2013, no less than 100[nbsp ]000[nbsp ] posted workers, paid less than 5[nbsp ]euro an hour, were listed in defiance, of course, of our social rules and also at the expense of our virtuous companies. fraud and abuse which are detrimental to the very idea of europe, which is why i think the deal proposed here is going in the right direction, with increased controls, more cooperation between member states, this open list which has been mentioned, documents which can be claimed, the identification also - this is essential - of the false independent workers and, above all, the cascading liability of the subcontracting chain. more than a blemish, a fault, in my opinion, but as we know, the national resistance was enormous in the head of some member states: the fact that this joint responsibility is precisely limited to the construction industry and not extended to other problematic sectors [nbsp ] we have mentioned them, transport, cleaning or others. in my view, solidarity with all employers and workers would also mean going beyond mere cooperation between states and establishing a genuine european body of labour inspectors, with the task of checking and punishing offenders and with the means to do so. so i share the concerns that have been expressed - i conclude, mr president - by mr hughes about article 9, but i do not think that "throwing the baby out with the bath water" is the responsible attitude that is expected of us.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is by achieving real equality between workers in terms of wages, social protection and working conditions that we will build a europe of social progress. that is why we wanted the basic directive on secondment to be revised. we have not received it from the commission and the debate has been limited to an implementing directive, with an agreement which aims to limit abuse and attempts to circumvent the law. there are many cases on the ground, in our towns and cities, in many sectors of activity, and i think that the fact that more controls are being allowed by the member states and that there is a chain of responsibility for failing companies is a step forward. however, this useful agreement is minimalist and cannot be used as a pretext to reject any idea of revising the directive itself tomorrow. the fight against competition between workers and social dumping in europe is therefore far from over.
mr president, my colleagues have spoken and it is true that this interpretative directive on the posting of workers is making some progress. the fight against cascading subcontractors, which i myself initiated in the public procurement directive, is fundamental. the fight against social dumping is a necessity in europe today. the fact that we can make checks easier does not impede the movement of workers, mr schmidt. the workers must move freely in today's europe, of course, as in yesterday's, and perhaps more easily in tomorrow's. mobility is fundamental, but not under any conditions. because today, under the 1996 directive, this mobility is organizing social dumping. it is very clear that the priority in the next parliamentary term will be to change the basic directive so that taxes and social security laws are paid where the worker works, in the country where he works. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this. this is one of the fundamental battles of the next parliamentary term to restore the citizens' confidence in the european union.
in writing. mr president, the mobility of people and services in the european single market is a huge achievement. but unfair competition, fraud and social dumping through the abuse of the rules on posting threaten to undermine the broad support enjoyed by our companies and workers for the freedoms of the internal market. the agreement on the enforcement directive should ensure better monitoring of the rules. the commission will be able to use the information it has obtained from the member states to assess the legality of the secondment of workers and to combat the problems of letterbox companies and the selfemployed. it is good that for the first time a european minimum standard for the sanctioning of fraud in subcontracting chains is being introduced. member states will have the opportunity to incorporate accompanying control measures at national level where necessary. i call on the european commission to respect this flexibility in the face of new forms of abuse. the same applies to national general liability schemes which are more ambitious than the european minimum standard. the lines of communication between the national inspectorates are in many cases still lacking. the automation of data exchange will allow for much better monitoring of secondments. it is therefore of the utmost importance that the european commission ensures that all member states implement the agreement correctly.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by adopting this decision, the union is turning a former informal platform of public employment services into a formal and operational cooperation network. it is clear that job creation is not the responsibility of the public employment services but depends on the employment and growth policies initiated by the union and the member states, policies made more difficult by the current austerity. however, these services play a fundamental role in the fight against unemployment and in achieving the strategy 2020 targets of increasing the employment rate to 75%. in view of the situation in europe, where unemployment rates can reach 25% in some countries and regions, any initiative to strengthen coordination in this area should be encouraged. this network will enable initiatives based on benchmarking or benchlearning to compare and mutually enrich each other's implementation of employment policies, which contribute to reducing unemployment for all age groups, in particular vulnerable groups, and to reducing the duration of unemployment in order to combat structural unemployment and social exclusion. this network will contribute to the strengthening of public employment services and will aim to support in particular the most vulnerable social groups, to promote decent and sustainable work, to improve the functioning of the labour market in the union and its integration, and to promote voluntary geographical and occupational mobility on fair terms, in order to meet specific labour market needs. the network will help identify skills shortages and better match the skills of jobseekers with the needs of employers. you will thus find that the missions and objectives assigned to this network are ambitious, with a role of analysis, exchange, initiative and suggestion in the field of employment policy. to carry out these tasks fully, all member states must be represented at the table and good cooperation with other actors on the labour market must be possible. thus, the presence of all around the table was a vital point of our discussions. what interpretation should be given to the texts, to the legal bases, on the compulsory or voluntary nature of this network? our discussions have not been able to resolve the differences in legal interpretation between the council on the one hand and the commission and parliament on the other. the proof: the council intends to attach to the agreement a unilateral declaration specifying its interpretation, namely participation by all, but on a voluntary basis. in this context, the employment committee of the european parliament proposes that the agreement should also be accompanied by, without calling into question, its interpretation, namely that participation by all, on a compulsory basis, is the only guarantee of real added value to this formal network. even if we succeed in adopting a text without any clashes, i must stress that this is not conducive to building confidence between the two institutions in the context of codecision. good cooperation for the network, i said: the network is encouraged to cooperate, if necessary, but only on its own initiative, with the social partners, ngos, local and regional authorities and employment services and other stakeholders. cooperation also with the other institutions of the union, via the secretariat provided by the commission and an employment committee (emco) with observer status, which does not prevent, where necessary, meetings in restricted session. in addition, we have ensured in this decision that there is not only this cooperation with all the actors, but also the involvement, in the activities of the network, of all the public employment services in the member states whose employment responsibilities are managed at subnational institutional levels, such as belgium. ladies and gentlemen, this agreement is the result of a good initiative by the european commission and a strong commitment by parliament and the council to achieve it during this parliamentary term, despite their differences of opinion. i would like to take this opportunity to thank my fellow rapporteurs and our committee chair, mrs pervenche berès, whose experience and tenacity are beyond compare, as well as the committee secretariat and the various collaborators. in conclusion, this new european social policy tool - which is rare enough to be highlighted - will give new impetus to the fight against unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and the fight against social exclusion.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the need for a strengthened and coordinated fight against unemployment at european level and for the effective and rapid implementation of the youth guarantee is obvious and has been mentioned in this debate. i would also like to thank the various speakers for their support. as regards the amendments tabled for vote, i suggest that we do not support them because the spirit of these amendments is largely embedded in our compromise and they would call the agreement into question. it is essential, as our commissioner has stressed, that the measure be adopted in this parliament so that the network can function fully and rapidly.
i would like to propose an oral amendment to amendments nos 314 and 316 tabled by members of the committee on agriculture and rural development and the epp. this means that we add the following sentence after the phrase 'including on form processing': 'provided that the respective operator produces for short supply chains only, as defined in article 2.1 (m) of regulation 1305/2013.' i ask for permission to put this oral amendment to the vote.

(applause) i would like to thank i begin my interlude in the netherlands, because in the first world war, a hundred years ago, so many belgians in vlamingen were killed in the war. the first world war was the first war that millions of europeans had to fight on an industrial scale. "flanders fields" may have today a heroic sound, but in reality, the places in flanders that can still be visited, are totally different. it was a reality of stinking graves, mustard gas and grenades, a reality of misery and death, which no one can imagine today. some writers are unable to call themselves authors. the first world war was the great war, which afterwards was no longer a prelude to a subsequent conflict that was so potentially devastating. in fact, i would say that the beginning was of the 20th century, a century that should never have been born as we look back at the tens of millions of people in europe who have found their end in it. we as politicians have all always had the urge to look at war with a geopolitical eye - actually taking a step back from the essence of war. war is not in my eyes about land recovery. it is also not always an armed struggle between countries. it's always a gruesome battle between people. something that rolled down the street in the eighties and that's life wasted. the essence of war is always the immense pain and suffering it causes. millions of families have been destroyed. i'm not going to let you get away with this. it's not like that. the definitive change in perception, in vision, in the world view, in the desire for ambition, before we have experienced a war, certainly in the war of 1914-1918, after we have had ambition. the war veterans have met with the condition that birds no longer fly in the spring, but in the fall. in front of them is the smell of hospital and air and something that gives peace and comfort. war is something we must continue to bear. war is not a geopolitical struggle, war is in the first instance the destruction of the lives of families and people. it is a huge step in european development that war for our own is become an aberration. thanks to the european project, we have now known nearly 70 years of unbroken peace. my generation knows only war from history books, from novels of that time. something in the glass of foreign countries is being published. nevertheless, dear colleagues, i think the war or the absence of it was once the only argument for europe and european integration. today that is no longer the case. let's be honest about it. we will not convince the younger generation just by pointing to a horrible but distant past. we need to explain to them how europe and european integration is a tool for a better future and to keep that peace on our continent, in our own countries, in the balkans and in our neighbourhood in ukraine. but we are not here today to reflect, i think, on the political arguments for further european integration. we are here to remember what binds us: the values of peace and cooperation. values which were not european values one hundred years ago. they were not european values, they became european values; they became european principles and they have become our binding principles over time. never again, never again, never again: two simple words expressing a whole history and a hope for the future and today we have the certainty that our children will not be sent into battle against each other. it is an absurd thought, it is an important thought, it is progress in the true sense of the word and therein lies also the greatest challenge i think for mankind. so my wish for europe is that we will be able to persevere with such progress. to secure such an immense leap forward; to leave our petty differences behind, to leave nationalism and populism behind and work on the basis of what binds us as europeans, because this simple insight is the driving force behind progress and is the engine of humanity. that is why this commemoration matters, even if none of us ever has to live through a war because war today between us has become unthinkable, has become impossible and has become also the reason why we must continue our quest: the quest for peace, the quest for a better future and that means the quest for europe. in writing. - in future, eu workers will be able to take their supplementary pension rights (pillar 2) with them. we are adopting legislation on this today, for those who move within the eu for a new job, as well as for frontier workers. this is a logical consequence of the principle of free movement and the european single market. if you move from flanders to work in a country such as france, for example, you must be able to assume that your supplementary pension rights will remain intact. the eu should be able to 'bundle' its rights and enjoy a single pension. this protection has been lacking until now for the supplementary pension of the second pillar, the occupational pensions paid by employers. such pension rights are not bundled, which may give rise to several separate pensions and the loss of tax benefits. this, of course, puts a brake on intra-european job mobility: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of workers are respected. as many member states encourage supplementary pensions to reduce the pressure on statutory pensions, we need to improve the conditions for safeguarding supplementary pensions within the eu. today brings it one step closer: this is the way to make work across the union worthwhile.
in writing. following negotiations between the european parliament and the council with the participation of the commission, the proposal under consideration provides legal certainty on supplementary pension rights for transnational mobility of workers. the rapporteur therefore recommends that it be approved without amendments.
in writing. food security has always played a central role in the european union's action. ensuring a high level of human, animal and plant health throughout the food chain is one of the objectives of the eu treaties, which over the years have led to the creation of a body of legislation comprising some 70 regulatory texts enabling the european agri-food industry to achieve internationally recognised safety and quality standards. the agri-food industry is the second largest in the union, with a total output in the food chain of around eur 750 billion per year and employing more than 48 million people, from primary production to catering and retail.
in writing. the eu's internal market is of vital importance to the european economy and no one wants to go back to the glory days of border controls. it goes without saying that adequate control of contagious animal diseases is the best precondition for the proper functioning of the internal market for trade in live animals, products of animal origin and foodstuffs. this is why this regulation is so important. at the same time, it is true that some member states or regions, more progressive than others, have succeeded in eradicating certain diseases in their territory. the regulation must strike a balance on this point. we must be able to benefit from a free market, but not from a free market in diseases. in this regard, article 169 on national measures for terrestrial animals should be amended to allow additional protection measures, provided, however, that they are based on a sound scientific basis and are not adopted for economic reasons such as disguised barriers to trade.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants.
in writing. in 2012, the european commission conducted a eurobarometer survey with telling results: 27[nbsp ]% of consumers considered a large number of non-food consumer products sold in europe to be unsafe. this is no doubt due to the massive import of "made in china" and other products manufactured to standards that are not always in line with european standards. rather than moving forward with a hypothetical new 'safety tested in europe' label, the european authorities would be well advised to strengthen the ce marking, as it is understood by consumers: a real guarantee of product safety and not just an indicator of a product's compliance with european legislation. that is why i voted against amendments nos 18, 19 and 60 to the schaldemose report. i welcome, however, the adoption of two key proposals: one to pay particular attention to vulnerable consumers, especially young children, who sometimes confuse toys with food. and the adoption of a quality standard, namely the mandatory indication of the country of origin for non-food products. this is the best way to showcase european know-how and to strengthen consumer confidence in the single market.
in writing. we want to make 'made in' labels compulsory for goods sold on the european market. we have also proposed tougher penalties for companies selling potentially dangerous products. enhancing product safety and increasing market surveillance rules: two objectives for greater protection of the european consumer. an effective single market requires two essential components: safety for consumers and a level playing field for businesses. the advances we are proposing tonight meet both of these objectives.

in writing. commodity markets are fundamentally different from pure and simple financial markets. while it is possible to live a lifetime without being directly affected by the price of stocks and bonds, it is impossible to live a lifetime without being affected by the price of food and energy. commodity derivatives, in the form of futures contracts, anticipate on the financial markets. the raw materials markets have developed without taking into account the legitimate needs of producers and consumers for raw materials, agricultural products and energy in order to guard against the impact on prices of factors beyond their control. nevertheless, the evolution of financial markets over the last ten years has been such that commodities have joined stocks and bonds as 'investment assets'.
in writing. the commission's drafting proposals for the markets in financial instruments directive and regulation (mifid and mifir) contain provisions explicitly designed to meet the need for the supervision and regulation of financial markets in relation to commodities. these proposals provide for specific position limits or alternative arrangements (article 59) for commodity derivatives, which is a positive step if the overall objective is to facilitate price setting and effective hedging of price risks to producers and consumers and, therefore, to prevent and correct asset bubbles and other distortions. as a necessary complement to position limits, the proposal introduces obligations to report positions by category of trader to the market and to regulators (article 60). the commission also notes that the current full exemption from mifid for commodity traders has been removed. these measures are in the right direction, but more is needed and can be done. to this end, your rapporteur for opinion believes that three general issues need to be addressed by the european parliament in the context of the mifid/mifir review.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no[nbsp]638/2004 on community statistics relating to the trading of goods between member states, as regards the conferral of delegated powers and implementing powers on the commission for the adoption of certain measures, the provision of information by the customs administration, the exchange of confidential data between member states and the definition of the statistical value.
in writing. the completion of the single market is a key priority for all european institutions, in the interests of competitiveness, growth and financial stability. whether to mitigate risk or to ensure a competitive environment for post-trade services, it is necessary to look at existing models of central securities depositories (csds) across the european union. we need to assess the suitability of existing models for the future development of the single market. one of the most immediate developments is the introduction of the ecb's target2securities (f2s) system, which is due to be launched in 2015. although historically there was only one csd for each member state, with the introduction of t2s it is now possible to see how a more streamlined and integrated model can develop.
in writing. the possibility of supplementing or replacing the steering wheel mark with electronic tags should be further encouraged as it facilitates inspections of ships calling at union ports and makes it possible to combat counterfeiting more effectively (article [nbsp ] 11). in addition, it is necessary to ensure that market surveillance measures remain proportionate to the objective pursued, in particular with regard to the sampling required by member states for the purpose of carrying out checks (article 27). finally, it is proposed to further specify the procedure for delegated acts (article [nbsp ]37) which the commission may use to amend the list of international conventions requiring flag state approval for equipment to be placed on board ships flying its flag and to update the references to european and international standards set out in annex iii to the directive.
in writing. the ncl introduces a simplified regulatory framework for products and allows for a more consistent application of technical standards, which will help to improve the functioning of the single market by ensuring equal treatment of non-compliant products and economic operators and equivalent assessment for notified bodies on the union market. i believe that alignment with the ncl will strengthen producer and consumer confidence, through clarification of the obligations of economic operators, and will provide member state authorities with more effective tools to carry out market surveillance checks, which will lead to an overall reduction in non-compliant and dangerous products on the market.
in writing. i fully agree with the main lines of the regulation proposed by the commission. the rapporteur, however, proposes several amendments in his draft report. it seems appropriate, in particular, to define clearly the scope of the proposed amending regulation, which is not intended to modify either the internal division of tasks within a common court or the specific rules on recognition and enforcement which the agreement on the common court might contain. special attention should also be paid, within the legal framework of a common court, to the rules applicable to third-country defendants, who are not generally covered by the brussels i rules. i agree with the adoption of the proposed legislation as soon as possible, since it is not controversial and the entry into force of the agreement on the unified patent court depends on it.

in writing. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), signed in 1973, aims to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not endanger their survival. the species covered by cites are grouped into three lists in its annexes, each list corresponding to a distinct degree of protection. council regulation (ec) no 338/97 aims to protect species of wild fauna and flora by controlling trade in them. it lays down provisions for the import, export and re-export of, and trade within, the union in specimens of species listed in its four annexes.
in writing. piracy has increased since 2004. this is why the european union launched operation atalanta in 2008 to combat piracy in the region. from 2009, the tugboats began to take military personnel or private armed security groups on board, which reduced the number of ships hijacked but increased the operational costs of the fleet. the current protocol contains a clause which provides that in exceptional circumstances relating to piracy, which force the fleet to leave the indian ocean, the two parties will examine the possibility of applying a pro rata temporis payment, upon individual request of the shipowners. the new protocol is in line with the objectives of the ppps. it maintains the european presence in the field of long-distance fishing and the fishing opportunities in this region of the indian ocean, contributes to the sustainability of fishing grounds and strengthens cooperation between the european union and seychelles. in view of the above, the rapporteur considers that the new protocol is balanced and beneficial for both parties and therefore recommends its approval.

in writing. the adopted regulation further harmonises, clarifies and strengthens the common rules for decision-making on noise-related operating restrictions at eu airports, such as the prohibition of night flights. these rules, which are based on principles endorsed by the international civil aviation organisation (icao), known as the 'balanced approach', cover in particular the assessment and management of aircraft noise and are designed to determine the most cost-effective way to deal with aircraft noise at each airport. the regulation applies only to the largest airports with traffic exceeding 50[nbsp ]000 civil aircraft movements per year and does not set specific noise thresholds, which remain the responsibility of national or local authorities.
in writing. - i welcome these new arrangements as they call for greater involvement of local authorities and residents in decision-making in this area, thus making the decision-making process more open and transparent and thus increasing the acceptance of measures. at eu level, we have proposed a balanced approach to noise-related decisions, with objective and measurable criteria to help in decision-making. at the same time, the eu parliament was able to ensure that the final decision on aviation noise reduction measures is taken exclusively by local authorities and on the basis of their national and, where appropriate, regional noise legislation and agreements. the eu commission cannot therefore, as originally proposed, call the measures into question. it can only review the procedure but not the content of the decision. this ensured that the principle of subsidiarity was upheld and that the eu commission was not involved. the noise measures at bierset airport are particularly exemplary, as they have created an excellent noise-reducing infrastructure in close cooperation with local residents. this has economic, social and environmental added value for the whole region and therefore bierset airport has always been mentioned in the debate, including by the european commission, as a prime example.
in the context of the 'airport package' on the (expansion of) airport capacity, the european commission has decided to adapt european legislation on noise emissions. it has based its proposal entirely on the 'balanced approach' of the international civil aviation organization (icao), which, despite its name, is anything but balanced. this approach does not focus on reducing noise, pollution, health and safety risks, but on the economic interests of commercial aviation, a handful of companies with a strong lobby. nothing in the legislation can prevent the european commission from circumventing the night flight ban for the economic interests of a number of companies. despite the improvements made by the european parliament to the original commission proposal (e.g. by including a paragraph on health damage), the new regulation will not improve the situation of people living near airports. this is the exact opposite of what european legislation should do, which is to ensure that all options remain available to guarantee the right to a healthy and quiet living environment.
in writing. the designation of a european capital of culture is widely followed by all european citizens. the chosen city becomes the nerve centre of the citizens' gathering, enabling everyone to enrich themselves by feeding on other crops present in the territory of the union. this is a major element of democratic learning. culture is the cement of positive identities, what defines both the individual and the collective, what makes us exist, as men and as peoples. it is education, training, openness to others and openness to knowledge. it is also a major driver of wealth and employment. creativity is the heart of innovation and innovation is the heart of development. we should seize every opportunity to develop the potential of a sector that generates jobs and income, especially for young people.
in writing. the rules for selecting european capitals established in 2006 will expire in 2019. given the long time-consuming nature of the current selection procedure, it was necessary to try to establish new rules for the period after 2020 by the end of 2013.
in writing. in view of the weaknesses identified by the commission in the first regulation, the provisions of this regulation for the protection of cetaceans will need to be revised before the end of 2015 to ensure that they are relevant and effective. on this basis, the commission shall, if appropriate, consider a comprehensive legislative proposal to be submitted to the european parliament and the council to ensure the effective protection of cetaceans, including through the use of regionalisation. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in order to update the technical specifications and conditions of use of sound-absorbing devices, including the corresponding signal and application characteristics, with a view to adapting the regulation to technical and scientific progress. the commission will allow sufficient time for the implementation of these adaptations. the power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the commission for a period of up to four years.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. better enforcement is needed to combat unfair competition and abuse. fraud must be dealt with forcefully. both workers and employers have benefited from greater transparency and legal certainty. in this context, closer cooperation and exchange of information between member states are particularly important. that is why i support this agreement. however, this is only one element of what should be a multifaceted approach. performance monitoring is essential for an efficient response to abuses. belgium, for example, is far from a good student in this area. the fragmentation of the social inspection services is an old wound. the federal government is unable to cope with the inefficient web of as many as ten separate social inspection services. my party, the n-va, therefore calls for a single social inspection service with specialised teams. the elimination of the wage cost handicap also remains a priority. the parties which are most vocal in calling for the fight against social dumping are precisely the same parties which have for years blocked structural reforms to make our economy competitive again. reducing labour costs is crucial to our competitiveness and absolutely necessary if our companies are to compete internationally on a level playing field.
in writing. - the ability to provide services across borders is an important european achievement, especially for border regions. the posting of workers is part of this and is regulated by the posting of workers directive. unfortunately, member states are still very hesitant to check compliance with this directive. this will allow abuse by circumventing existing rules and will not lead to sanctions against the companies. i therefore very much welcome the fact that this directive will strengthen the monitoring of compliance. the commission has also proposed that the member states designate a competent authority to monitor compliance with the posting of workers directive and that information on working and employment conditions be exchanged more easily between member states, while respecting data protection. in addition, service providers from another member state must provide a declaration, including the identity of the service provider, the number of workers posted, the expected duration and the address of the workplace. this will make it easier to control. i also welcome the fact that additional measures can be introduced by the member states to prevent the direct subcontractor from being able to avoid liability due to the lack of transparency in the subcontracting chain in the case of subcontracting, which is particularly common in the construction sector.
in writing. i said yesterday in the plenary debate that social dumping is seriously damaging to the economic health of europe. the diversion of the application of the posting of workers directive is the best proof of this. in belgium alone, in 2013, no less than 100,000 posted workers, paid less than €5 an hour, were recorded, in defiance of the social rules applied in my country. that is why the european parliament's vote this afternoon in favour of the 'posting of workers' implementing directive is a good thing, whatever the extremes of the right and the left may think. substantial improvements were made to the text: the identification of 'independent falsehoods' and a wider margin of manoeuvre granted to states to carry out checks on the ground. to this must be added the cascading liability of contractors and subcontractors, unfortunately limited to the building sector. the introduction of a minimum wage in germany is anything but trivial and also part of the overall environment in which social europe is taking shape step by step. in conclusion: "it is better not to throw the baby with the bath water" and to put the book back on the shelf after the elections of 25 may.
in writing. - today, together with my green group, i voted in favour of the enforcement directive on the posting of workers. this new european legislation obliges all eu countries to better check that employers are following the law when posting workers across borders. authorities should be required to exchange information on malfunctions so that illegal mailbox businesses and forced pseudo-independence will soon be a thing of the past. countries should also inform workers of their rights when they are working in another country on a temporary basis on behalf of their employer. only good european agreements prevent the free movement of firms from leading to underpayment, exploitation and unfair competition. these agreements will help to tackle problems such as social dumping. i therefore voted against certain amendments which were intended to undermine the agreement reached between the council, the commission and the european parliament. i am convinced that this new directive will improve the practical situation for posted workers and that there will be no more excesses like those in flamanville. i do think that there is a need for a kind of social europol which can fight crossborder crime and violations of european social agreements more effectively.
in writing. i abstained, torn between the progress achieved by the socialists (sapin and di rupo) and the weakness of the rest of the text. the directive on the posting of workers already organises unfair competition between social protection systems. this competition is all the more exacerbated by the fact that more and more companies are abusing the directive to make it a veritable social dumping tool. this puts workers in economic unemployment in our country, who are replaced by exploited and underpaid workers. we can't accept that. beyond today's vote, it will be essential to revise the directive by highlighting a major principle: taxes and social laws must be paid in the country where the service is provided.
in writing. the purpose of the recast is to approximate the laws of the member states as regards the conditions for compensation of the owner of the property to be returned, by placing the burden of proof on the owner and not by referring this question to the laws of the member states. the owner of the property will thus have to show that he acted with sufficient diligence when acquiring it, that is, that he took sufficient steps to ensure its lawful origin. since the owner is usually an actor in the art market, it seems quite natural that he should be required to have done everything possible to ensure the legality of the cultural property before granting him compensation.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to point out the challenges posed by the enormous plastic mountain. as many as 8 billion plastic bags end up in the european environment as waste every year. it is clear that this is causing great damage to the environment, particularly in our seas. a european target to reduce use could provide a major impetus. at present, there are huge differences between member states. for example, flanders is already showing very good results: the use of plastic carrier bags has already been reduced by more than 86% compared with 2003, which puts us in the european lead and means that we are achieving the first objective with virtually no additional effort. however, there is still room for improvement. i would also like to stress that the measures proposed by the european parliament are in line with the polluter pays principle. but this file is only part of the puzzle. the proper implementation and enforcement of the waste directive remains very important and the packaging directive has a lot of potential. this legislation dates back to 1994 and needs to be updated. as the current target of at least 22.5% collection is being met almost across the eu, this figure could rise considerably.
in writing. those who have seen reports on what scientists and navigators call the "7th continent", this giant patch of plastic waste floating on the pacific ocean, 100 times the size of belgium, can only agree with the ambitious proposals in ms. auken's report. yes, it was important to vote for amendment no 34, which allows member states who wish to ban single-use plastic bags. i also supported other common sense measures, in particular the commitment by member states to gradually replace very light plastic bags with handles used for packaging foodstuffs such as fruit, vegetables or confectionery with handles made from recycled paper or with biodegradable plastic bags. because it is in our everyday purchases that we can make a difference, already by starting to generalize the payment of reusable bags, at 5 or 10 cents. to establish a win-win logic between traders and consumers. it is still the best policy with consumer awareness, environmental education to achieve the goal of 80[nbsp]% less disposable plastic bags by 2019.
in writing. - on average, each european uses 200 plastic bags a year. many of these disposable bags end up in the plastic soup that floats on the sea. every year, millions of marine animals die from plastic in their stomachs. the green group is now taking a lead in tackling this major environmental problem at european level. the report voted on today, for example, sets binding european targets to halve the use of single-use plastic bags within three years and to reduce it by 80% within five years. member states are required to charge a cost price for plastic carrier bags in the food sector and are encouraged to do so for the non-food sector. progressive countries, such as belgium, have already shown that putting a price tag on the use of disposable bags drastically reduces their use. these measures will have a positive effect in the short term and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european parliament votes this afternoon on a directive on the use of thin plastic bags. our legislation requires member states to reduce the use of polluting plastic bags by 80% by 2019. when we consider that each european uses 200 plastic bags a year, 180 of which are not or only slightly reused, we can see the extent of the environmental consequences of this.
in writing. while respecting the sovereignty of the member states over their territorial seas, a key objective of this proposal is to achieve an increased level of cooperation between member states in frontex-coordinated operations, which always require authorisation from the member states concerned by an action on their territorial sea. while the primary responsibility for ensuring the establishment of appropriate asylum and border management systems lies with the states, the feu treaty, as well as the stockholm programme, requires a greater level of solidarity and a fair sharing of responsibilities between the eu institutions as well as the member states in the development of the common european asylum system and the gradual establishment of an integrated management system for the external borders. the current legal framework of the european union already offers a range of tools and instruments for responsibility-sharing and solidarity that can be useful in addressing protection gaps and weaknesses in member states' asylum and border management systems and in improving the overall quality of the common european asylum system.

in writing. while it is important to ensure that the regulation under consideration covers emissions from shipping as consistently as possible, it is also essential to focus on the essentials and to limit implementation costs and administrative burdens. similarly, companies should not be obliged to publish sensitive and potentially misleading information. we therefore propose to exclude transportation from other useful climate-related information, as this data is not related to emission measurements. the high cost of fuels already provides a strong incentive for the maritime market to improve its energy efficiency, and the energy efficiency of transport in real-world conditions is a much more complex issue, which cannot be addressed without knowledge of the specific market conditions that dictate the decisions of shipowners and ship operators. the actual energy efficiency of a journey and its impact on social welfare cannot be determined without knowing the cargoes available, their mass in relation to weight, weather conditions, applicable prices, geographical and other constraints, delivery time, etc.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not distorted by the introduction of new species. the eu is home to over 12 000 species that are alien to their natural environment, of which about 15% are invasive. the asian tiger mosquito, the asian ladybug, the giant bear claw, and the japanese centipede are striking examples. the problem was in the news last week when the raccoon was first filmed in the wild in flanders. i therefore believe that the european parliament has rightly been calling for european legislation for a long time. this is a case in which european cooperation offers concrete added value. invasive alien species have a particularly damaging impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, causing considerable damage to human health, agriculture and infrastructure with significant economic consequences (estimated at €12 billion per year across the eu). fortunately, during the negotiations we were able to get rid of a system of national exceptions, which would seriously impede the effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and enforceability of the legislation. i myself have always been keen to see the respect for animal welfare in this case. i am pleased that this has been firmly established in the legislation, thanks in part to amendments of my own making.
in writing. - for centuries, new exotic plant and animal species have been arriving on the european continent. most of these are harmless, but about 15 percent of these organisms pose a serious threat to the continent's native diversity, causing an estimated average of 12 billion euros of damage each year. member states have tried to limit the impact of these harmful alien species but have not been able to act quickly and adequately. the bill to tackle this crossborder problem at european level is therefore not a moment too soon. i was therefore astonished when the environmental management committee (envi) of the parliament, led by the socialist rapporteur pavel poc, decided to adopt an open list of exceptions per member state, in order to safeguard the fur processing industry. i could not vote for this as a green mep because it completely undermines the common european approach. fortunately, the negotiations with the council of environment ministers have opted for a more differentiated approach, whereby the most threatening organisms are no longer allowed to be released, imported or traded throughout the eu. that is why i can vote in favour now. however, it is incomprehensible that genetically modified organisms have not been included in the legislation, despite clear evidence that their unintended spread has persistent and harmful effects.
in writing. the draft proposal consists essentially of a list of eee of union concern, the adverse consequences of which require concerted action at union level. this list will be drawn up by the commission in cooperation with the member states. species listed as union concern will be banned, but some limited derogations will be provided for. member states will have to take measures to ensure that species are not introduced, traded, held, cultivated or released into the union. those species may have damaging effects on all or part of the union, but it is justified, given the seriousness of their impact, to seek assistance from other member states of the union.

for as much as 75%. and we know that the banks are keeping their fingers crossed, among other things, to meet all kinds of capital requirements and so on. smes therefore face difficulties in obtaining financing. this is shown, for example, by the fact that greek, spanish and italian smes who go to a bank have only a 33% to 50% chance of actually getting a loan. in germany, the figure is as high as 87%. this means that the countries most affected are also having a harder time organising their economic recovery. what is on the table is an important step forward, provided that a number of qualitative requirements are met. the new rules allow both retail and institutional investors to enter an infrastructure project, but that cannot work if investors can withdraw their money at any time. so it was important to get that organized. investors will only be able to withdraw their money at a specified end date of their investment, i.e. early, but under very strict conditions and that must also be clearly communicated in advance. in addition, eltifs have to comply with certain requirements set out in the regulations, in particular the types of long-term assets in which they can be invested, the companies they can invest in, for example infrastructure, transport, renewable energy projects, how their money should be distributed to reduce risks, and so on. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. finally, it is important that there are no links with tax havens. we as parliament have done our job, it is now up to the council to take a swift stand.

financing was largely dependent on banks, banks that had gotten into trouble. one of the things that is being advocated is to look at how we can provide a more diversified form of financing for small businesses and also for long-term infrastructure projects. this is very necessary at the moment, since governments too are having enormous problems in securing the necessary funds to bring such projects to a successful conclusion. i think this proposal is very timely. at a time when the economy is starting to pick up again, it could provide an additional boost to attract this type of activated at retail level through institutional investors, who now have an easier time making effective long-term commitments through these funds so that, for example, road infrastructure, rail infrastructure, but also school building and so on can get more, more incentives than they do today. at the same time, we also note that we have also made some provisions for companies to make it - i'm the reporter. - we all know that waste is a resource with potential. commission research has shown that full compliance with the eight eu waste legislation, including the regulation we are discussing today and hopefully strengthening in the future, could increase the turnover of the european waste treatment industry by €42 billion by 2020. that could create 400,000 additional jobs. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal waste shipments, and it is therefore important to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented. the point is to keep waste here and not to dump it unnecessarily in third world countries, where it is treated indiscriminately, in antisocial conditions and sometimes with the use of child labour. the illegal recycling of waste is a serious problem. the commission calculated that if only 1% of waste shipments are illegal, then 2.8 million tonnes of waste are illegally exported every year. the european environmental implementation and enforcement network (impel) and the people who do the checks in ports estimate that about 25% of all waste shipments are effectively illegal. that would mean that some 70 million tons of waste are illegally exported every year. the people in the field also show or tell us that the controls vary greatly from one member state to another. some member states, such as france, carry out virtually no checks. others, like poland, are quite good performers. the commission put forward a proposal in july last year to strengthen the existing regulation on waste shipments. i was appointed rapporteur at the beginning of october 2013. i immediately went to speak to the authorities who are carrying out the checks. i visited the port of antwerp, where i had a very interesting meeting with the customs authorities, the public waste management company, the federal environmental police and also the local magistrate responsible for combating environmental crime. even in that first contact i noticed that the people in the field welcomed the commission's proposal with open arms, but they also had to add some additional elements to this proposal which would increase their impact. i am able to present a very strong dossier today, partly on the basis of those talks and with the very good cooperation with the shadow rapporteurs. it is a strong dossier, which we also took to the council of ministers and in which we finally reached a compromise. the new regulation before us, which we hope to adopt soon, contains a number of important elements: the first. all member states should draw up a risk-based control plan detailing a strategy and objectives for controls on waste shipments and specifying the means to be used for this purpose. there is therefore a need for detailed inspection plans. the second. the inspection services will have more scope to check whether a shipment is legal or not. this means that even without any factual suspicion, the inspectors concerned can request additional information to verify the nature of the shipment, i.e. whether or not it is waste, or its destination, i.e. whether or not the destination is a place where something is being processed in a responsible manner. the third. member states should also provide for a minimum number of physical inspections of installations or waste shipments in accordance with agreed objectives and based on a sound risk assessment. 4. other a harmonised protocol for the collection, recording and reporting of data on the enforcement of the regulation and a comparative table for customs and waste codes will be established. the fifth. in addition, there will be more information exchange between inspection services on the punishment of offences across europe, with a view to greater harmonisation in the future. the sixth. (this was a difficult point in the negotiations with the member states) the monitoring plans must be made public in accordance with the 2003 directive on public access to environmental information, which we adopted in 2004. the directive has several aspects, active and passive dissemination, and we as a parliament wanted to go further in this respect. we have had to reach a compromise with the council on this. that was a difficult point in the council of ministers and it strikes me that in a great many discussions on environmental legislation we still have to push member states hard for openness. that is a sad case. another point of discussion was the date on which the new regulation was to enter into force. we have had to compromise on that too. we wanted to move faster as a parliament. finally, a compromise has been reached between the time proposed by the council and the time proposed by us. this regulation shall therefore enter into force on 1 january 2016. the first inspection plans should be available as of 1 january 2017. i repeat, it is a compromise, but i believe that we can present a good piece of work here and i hope that the people in the field will also be able to reap the benefits, so that they can do their work in an excellent way. i thank all the members who have taken part in this exercise and i hope that we shall soon be able to adopt this regulation by a large majority.

member of the commission. - mr president, honourable members, i am replying on behalf of my colleague, commissioner kallas. mr[nbsp ]simpson, i fully share the concerns you raise in your questions. member states and the commission must apply the road transport acquis correctly to protect the rights of those working in the transport sector and to ensure road safety and the proper functioning of the internal market. effective enforcement of european union legislation is important, particularly when it comes to the conditions that road haulage operators must fulfil. one of these conditions is stable and effective establishment. letterbox companies should not be set up or, if they exist, they must be closed down. however, the commission depends on information from the member states when it comes to the number of letterbox companies closed down. according to the relevant regulation, member states must report every two years their enforcement activities, including the withdrawal of road haulage licences. the commission received the first reports in december 2013. it has started analysing them and it will soon report on its conclusions. member states who have failed to report may soon face infringement procedures. our preliminary analysis shows that member states are finding it difficult to enforce certain parts of the regulation and other parts of the regulation are insufficient – for instance when member states must only check whether undertakings satisfy the criterion of stable and effective establishment once every five years until the end of 2014 but not thereafter. the commission therefore considers that this requirement could be strengthened. coming to your second and third questions about cross-border enforcement and controls, the commission, together with the member states, is working with great persistence to improve their effectiveness. member states have to carry out concerted checks with other member states at least six times a year. to give enforcement officers access to information about undertakings abroad, member states have to connect their register with the european register of road transport undertakings. several member states have not yet connected their national registers to the european register of road transport undertakings. this hampers cross-border enforcement. the commission has started infringement procedures against these members states – seven of these are still pending. the commission also funds projects to harmonise the training of control officers. the trace project for digital tachograph checks has now been completed and the closer project on a broader set of topics started just a short time ago. to reach a common understanding of applicable road transport legislation, the commission works with member states to adopt guidance and clarification notes on existing rules. twelve of these are already available. in addition, the commission requests member states to carry out individual checks on road haulage undertakings whenever it obtains evidence those companies are failing to meet their obligations, including the one on stable and effective establishment. most recently, the commission has taken action following a written question submitted by a member of the european parliament, ole christensen. concerning your fourth and final question, the enforcement of driving time and rest periods by member states is being progressively harmonised. the enforcement directive sets minimum requirements for controls and defines a common range of infringements against social rules. it also provides member states with tools to target checks and make them more efficient. national enforcement authorities can rely on data from the digital tachograph to check compliance with driving times and rest periods. the tachograph is gradually being improved and made more tamper-proof. as mentioned before, the commission cooperates with member states to better enforce driving time and rest periods. this includes the adoption of guidance notes, clarification notes, recommendations and training manuals for enforcers. to conclude, the commission strives to guarantee efficient and uniform enforcement practices throughout europe in cooperation with the member states, which are responsible for day-to-day enforcement. effective enforcement is an essential part of a well-functioning road transport market. it is not easy, but we are committed to improving the situation which members have painted. thank you for your interest in this important topic. i look forward to the debate.

in writing. it is essential to make the protection of human life a top priority. in kampala, the states parties to the icc reached a compromise on the crime of aggression. however, the difficulties in implementing it are regrettable. the court of justice of the european union (the 'court') is the supreme court of the european union, and its jurisdiction extends to all the courts of the member states of the european union. at present, only 12 states parties, including belgium, have ratified the amendments relating to the crime of aggression; which makes me say that the kampala declaration is a reflection of the challenges that the icc has to face, namely: its impact on victims of crime, the necessary cooperation of states in the investigation and arrest of the accused, and complementarity by intervening only as a last resort. it is therefore urgent that the eu takes the lead in bringing the kampala amendments on the crime of aggression into force.
in writing. as defined by the assembly of states parties meeting in kampala, the crime of aggression is the planning, preparation, instigation or commission of an act by a state of using armed force against the sovereignty, territorial integrity or political independence of another state. acts of aggression shall include, inter alia, invasion, military occupation or annexation by the use of force and the blockade of ports or coasts, if by their nature, gravity and extent such acts are considered to be manifest violations of the charter of the united nations. i fully support this resolution which aims to recall that the crime of aggression is still commonplace throughout the world and to condemn the impunity enjoyed by too many criminals who commit these crimes. the entry into force of the international criminal court (icc) in 2002 ushered in a new era of global accountability and ushered in the end of impunity. it also considers that the kampala conference, like this resolution, is an opportunity to underline our collective determination that crimes against humanity should no longer go unpunished.

there are ways. there are simple ways, but you have to give yourself the will to use them. the first way is through rules, binding objectives. you will have to debate binding climate targets, energy efficiency targets, resource efficiency targets with the commission and the council. it's by setting yourself binding goals that things move. it is not just the greens who say this, it is the companies that work in this sector who say it. no binding goals, no investments. it's all about the money. it's as simple as that. secondly, if there is any structural reform to be done, it is to re-engineer our tax systems. you will tell me that this is for the member states. no, we have to do it together. today, our tax systems are both socially unfair, economically counterproductive and environmentally destructive. we must make a flat taxation review and i know that there is a rule of unanimity, but we cannot continue in this way. if you want a tax system that is more conducive to investment, you have to change it radically. the last thing i want to say to you is that as long as the casino economy remains open for business, don't expect the cash that all the central banks of the world put into the financial system to end up in the economy. the bank of england has been flooding the uk with liquidity for years, the european central bank with a little less enthusiasm. where does this money end up today? they finance bubbles on the price of assets, whether real estate assets or movable assets. this cash is not invested in the economy. because obviously while it's easy to make a profit without working, by speculating, you, as so-called financial investors, are not going to invest in the real economy because it's difficult, because it involves taking risks, risks that will not be borne by the taxpayer. these are the structural reforms we want. we are in favour of structural reforms but not the ones you propose. answer is "blue cardboard". mr schaffhauser, the question you are asking is a valid one. to some extent, what we are seeing is already a more modest form of quantitative easing in continental europe than what we see in the uk. that cash must be made available, yes, but do not forget that these are loans that will have to be repaid. of course, investments must be profitable. what i observe is that in reality europe does not suffer from a lack of available capital. the problem is a problem of allocation of this capital. this capital is not being invested where it should be. in other words, he goes more into speculation, especially real estate - you see it in paris, london, brussels and elsewhere - and in the stock markets. we therefore believe that it is better to redirect available liquidity to where it can be invested productively rather than always adding additional liquidity. so, obviously, how much? it's something to look at. but let us ask ourselves the question of allocation of resources before we always want to create additional resources. europe is a rich continent today, let us not forget, but its capital is simply not allocated in the best possible way.

in writing. i welcome the reports on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. the european globalisation adjustment fund helps workers who have been the victims of the closure of a large company or the relocation of a large production site outside the eu to reintegrate into the labour market through targeted measures. the annual allocation of the fund is set at a maximum annual amount of eur 150 million for the financial period 2014 to 2020. the globalisation adjustment fund complements the esf and is an important tool for reintegration into the european labour market, which is undergoing rapid change as a result of globalisation. the measures financed include, inter alia, vocational guidance, vocational training and traineeships, assistance in starting up independent activities, renting of the production site and payment of the rent for the duration of the project, travel allowance, application grant, flat-rate residence allowance and traineeship allowance, and support after starting a new activity. these measures are designed to promote the workers in the most targeted way possible. the fund is deliberately targeted at individual investors and is not intended to restructure companies or sectors.

in writing. - i am pleased that a project has been set up to support the reintegration into the labour market of 633 workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis in 142 companies active in the manufacture of metal products in spain. the economic crisis has had a severe impact on these different sectors across the european union. the decline in industrial production has had an impact on employment. almost 600 000 jobs were lost in spanish industry between 2008 and 2012, including 150 000 in the manufactured metal products sector. these job losses represent respectively 24% of total employment in industry and 35% of total employment in the metalworking sector. the loss of jobs in the metal products sector was even greater in the comunidad valenciana. indeed, the number of jobs in the metalworking sector in this region decreased from 35 868 in 2008 to 20 873 in 2012, representing a decline of 43%, eight percentage points more than at national level.
in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to help workers who have lost their jobs as a result of developments in world trade and the victims of the financial crisis. the request, submitted by spain, concerns redundancies in the steel industry. spain is one of the member states most severely affected by the crisis. the latter has, inter alia, led to a decline in demand and production of metals and metal products. manufacturing of metal products decreased by 23.3% in 2009 compared to the previous year and by 36.6% between 2008 and 2013; the sector's turnover decreased by 38,5% in the period from 2008 to 2012 and job losses represent 43% of total employment in the metallurgy sector. the aim is to help 300 of the 633 redundant employees in 142 enterprises in the comunidad valenciana region. the aid will amount to eur 1 019 184 and will help to co-finance active labour market measures focusing on vocational guidance, placement, training, etc. this request has my support and that of the european parliament.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report which will make it possible to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for the 633 redundancies at comunidad valenciana/metal. these redundancies will only worsen the unemployment situation in a region which is already particularly fragile, given that the metal products sector accounts for 25.4% of regional industrial employment. the number of jobs in the metalworking sector there has risen from 35,868 in 2008 to 20,873 in 2012 - a decline of 43%. while european financial aid to redundant workers should be more dynamic and provided as quickly and efficiently as possible, a european strategy for the steel industry is also needed. it's vital today.
in writing. i welcome the granting of a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund, which the belgian authorities had requested from the eu in the wake of the redundancies at the assembly plant and at ford genk's suppliers. the fund was set up to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the fund finances personalised measures for the reintegration of jobseekers, encourages self-employment and business creation, provides mobility grants and grants for disadvantaged or elderly workers. the redundancies which have been made and those which are likely to be made will have a serious impact not only on the labour market in the province of limburg but also on the whole of the flemish region. it is therefore gratifying that the eu has accepted belgium's request and is providing funds to support the displaced workers, in the hope that the measures taken will help them to secure permanent, long-term and thus stable employment.

for the greens/efa group mr president, i must be a very naive or a little bit optimistic on the edges from time to time, but i remember that in march 2011, after the fukushima disaster, the very pro-nuclear chancellor merkel said to herself: "you know, the energy transition is an environmental requirement and an economic opportunity for germany". and she went all in. i thought that after the ukraine crisis, all european leaders would have come to the conclusion that this is not only an environmental requirement and an economic opportunity, but also a strategic imperative. i therefore expected the council, which will be meeting shortly, to adopt the european parliament's position very easily. i would remind you of the delvaux report, adopted at the end of the previous parliamentary term, which stresses the need for a threefold objective, both ambitious and binding. because, as you know, i couldn't find the french equivalent of "what gets measured, gets done". and conversely, what is not measured is not done. we had binding targets for co2 reductions and for the share of renewable energy, and we are meeting them. we had a non-binding target for energy efficiency. and guess what happened next?
