(the president agreed to answer two 'blue card' questions) (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure)
answer is "blue cardboard". mr president, i believe that these are two absolutely crucial and well-founded questions. the first question, by mr rübig, concerns the industrial dimension. the energy transition project is first and foremost an industrial project. it is an industrial modernization site, but the production of equipment is also an industrial site. the question is therefore whether we want to promote industrial infrastructure inherited from the 19th and 20th centuries or build the industrial infrastructure of the 21st century. i agree with you that some sectors, which are extremely limited in number, would indeed be very exposed because of too rapid a transition and that these sectors must be protected. we agree. but we must not lump all industrial sectors together. the social question is again extremely well founded. this is a real problem and it is true that during the investment phase of the energy transition we have a rise in the cost of energy which, indeed, affects the weakest. how are we going to proceed? one way must be used in any case: progressive energy pricing, i.e. energy pricing which favours the poorest households fiscally . we wanted to try it in belgium and in some of the places where we greens are in power. this would eliminate the impact of the energy transition on these people, but it also means that we are raising the price of energy for those households who can afford it. that's the first part. the second part is based on the long-term financing of the energy transition, which will allow savings in the future. there are enough financiers in this house to answer this question: how can we anticipate the benefits of the energy transition and use those anticipated benefits to finance the transition?
president. - ladies and gentlemen, it is essential that the heads of government take their responsibility when they take decisions on friday. and let's hope they make decisions on energy and climate, the 2030 energy climate package. because if europe and the council do not take responsibility on friday, we will have a very big problem in lima or paris. then europe cannot say, we take our responsibility, and other parts of the world - i am thinking of china and the united states - ask to take that responsibility too. so now that responsibility must be taken. we drew important lines in the european parliament last year, in february of this year. it is not a question of the line of one group, because our group would like to see it be more ambitious. it is the line of a large majority in the european parliament. and it deals with three enforceable objectives at european level. you know them: the 40% reduction in co2 emissions, the 40% energy efficiency and the renewable energy. and on friday in the council - we heard that - about half the member states would be prepared to reduce emissions by at least 40%. and that 40% is extremely important, because that is what the european parliament wants, and it gives us some flexibility if we want to point out to others their responsibilities on the international stage. so please, let's go that way. but of course, it doesn't stop there. it's a whole package. in europe too, we must stop subsidizing fossil fuels and unconventional fossil fuels and we must also meet those other two objectives. oxfam recently calculated -- and this is a very important source -- that a target of 40 percent energy efficiency, 40 percent energy efficiency, would save every household, every household in the european union, 300 euros. so to say that there is a contradiction between energy efficiency and clear objectives, and the future, is not true at all. i call on the heads of government to take responsibility for this coming friday.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i wish to thank everyone very much for this debate. it was very wide ranging, touching upon various issues on the agenda of the european council. many speakers paid attention to climate and energy policy, which is an extremely important thing for europe but also for the rest of the world. i do not know whether i should say too much about it, because commissioner-designate cañete would be a better specialist in this field. but, if i just mention that this area is, if i should mention one, probably one of the biggest source of competitiveness – if we just manage to deal with climate policy and energy policy together and the most effective way. first or all there is an endless demand for clean technology solutions; there is also endless demand for non-food biofuels, renewables and, if we manage to regulate right things instead of wrong things, we could create incentives for the private sector to innovate and create new solutions to save energy, but also produce cleaner energy and cheaper energy. so, at the end of the day, here in europe we would have better energy for a better price and also technology to sell to other parts of the world. so, basically, as commissioner-designate cañete said in his hearings, we need a better energy market, fewer subsidies but a more unified market and we need better energy connections in order to allow energy to flow across the borders in order to maximise the efficiency of energy production. we also need better regulations for renewables in order to let them come into the market. unfortunately, at the moment we are suffering, for instance, some trade barriers within the european union, meaning that not all the member states allow the best and newest technology to come into their market because they want to protect their own market. i am sure that this house will not accept this kind of behaviour and it is surely one of the issues which will be on the agenda of the next commission. but before there is a next commission there is a european council meeting. i would just like to stop here and say that i will pass these messages from the members on to the current president of the commission, and i am sure we can come back to the industrial renaissance, which is very important for the speaker of the parliament who is the father of this concept in europe, and it is also one part of the climate and energy policy with which we are going to deal in the next commission.

the rapporteur. - madam president, normally the report on draft amending budget no 2/2014 which i am presenting to you should have been a mere formality. as provided for in the financial regulation, the commission presents each year a draft amending budget to budget the surplus resulting from the previous year's budgetary year, i.e. in this case the year 2013. i said, "normally". unfortunately, things are not normal. anyone who has any idea of the budgetary situation in the union knows that the payments situation is becoming critical, if not dramatic. based on the information available, there were over 23 billion unpaid debts at the end of 2013 and they would approach 30 billion today, if nothing is done. when i say unpaid, i mean very specifically that these are proper invoices which are waiting to be paid and which cannot be paid because there are not enough payment appropriations. this is totally abnormal. it is a real debt, real but hidden, whereas the union's budget must be in balance. this is also intolerable and i would ask the council if it remembers that it adopted a directive a short while ago which was addressed to the member states and which instructed them to demand that the invoices be paid within 30 days. does he understand what the current situation means for erasmus students, who will not receive the money agreed when they are entitled to receive it? does the council appreciate what it means for a state, a local authority or a regional authority, which is already facing a difficult budgetary situation, not to have its bills reimbursed? does he understand what it means for an sme or a research team not to receive the agreed amounts, when the staff has been hired, is in place and is to be paid? the situation has become so critical that the commission has decided to submit to the budgetary authority an amending budget no 3, in which it requests additional payment appropriations for a total amount of eur 4.8 billion. at the same time, it tabled several other draft amending budgets, in which it proposed, for the most part, to include in revenue the proceeds from fines and interest on late payment totalling some eur 5 billion. it is clear from the outset that the member states should not go out of their way to finance the additional payment appropriations in the event of an honourable agreement between the two arms of the budgetary authority. the committee on budgets has taken account of all these factors and has adopted two important strategic guidelines, which it asks our assembly to support unreservedly. firstly, we want to deal with all the draft amending budgets for the financial year 2014 together, i.e. as a whole, when negotiating with the council. the purpose of this block treatment is to prevent the council from rejecting requests for additional appropriations or rebates, but to retain for the benefit of the member states the additional revenue which has increased, almost miraculously, the initial revenue foreseen for the financial year. it is precisely in order to be able to deal with all the draft amending budgets in a single package that this report asks you to approve an amendment to draft amending budget no 2 presented by the commission. if this amendment is not approved, the council will have the power, because of the delay, to seize the surplus for the 2013 financial year for the benefit of the member states, thus depriving the union budget of the possibility of using it to untie the knot of unpaid invoices. the second important line adopted by the committee on budgets has already been expressed today in the organisation and agenda of our work: it is to reach agreement with the council on the amending budgets for 2014 before starting negotiations on the 2015 budget. this strategic choice, which was supported - i would like to stress this - by all the political groups in the committee on budgets, is necessary for us for two reasons. the first, as i said, is that there is an urgent need for additional appropriations. this urgency concerns both the beneficiaries, who are waiting for their bills to be paid, and the union itself, whose credit will be badly affected if it is not able to honour the commitments it has made. secondly, the 2015 budget, which we are voting on tomorrow, will not hold up if the 2014 budget, unchanged, leaves it with a backlog of unpaid debts of several billion. an agreement on the 2014 amending budget is therefore both an urgent necessity and a prerequisite for the adoption of a sustainable 2015 budget. it is for these reasons that i ask you to approve the report i am presenting to you today.

it is impossible to have investment and growth without fiscal discipline and it is – as you said, mr juncker – impossible to have economic growth in the future without good, sound public finances. i hope that mr katainen comes up with a plan as soon as possible. you are talking about eur 300 billion, mostly from repackaging, but you know what the problems are. the problem is that the investment gap today in europe is not eur 300 billion. the investment gap in europe is currently more than eur 800 billion. close to one trillion is lacking in investment – private mainly – in our infrastructure, in digital, in the energy grid, in transport and in innovation. i hope that, in the coming months, you can come forward with a credible strategy and a plan for closing that gap – but not in the traditional way of saying ‘yes, we will increase a little the amount of capital in european investment.’ you need to come forward with a credible strategy like delors did to create the internal market for consumer goods. we need a new way forward in the integration of the european union, in digital, in energy, in innovation and in our capital markets, which are not unified at the moment. that is what we are waiting for, and we need it as soon as possible. the second thing is: can this new structure work? we have always been in favour of coordination and clustering, and i hope it can work, but i have to tell you that i have doubts about it. in a marriage it is very clear: you do not decide everything together. in my marriage, i decide the questions of peace and war, and my wife does the finances, so there is a clear division of power, but i do not know whether appointing two commissioners for the stability pact is the way forward. i think it could be a source of problems, though i hope it is not because i am very much in favour of coordinating and clustering. i hope, in any case, that we will not see internal battles in your commission. we had a long deadlock in the european union with discussions between paris and berlin on the union’s future strategy. we cannot afford to have a deadlock because mr dombrovskis and mr moscovici have different opinions about the application of the stability pact and about future strategy. i want us to look at this question closely and i want you, mr juncker, to intervene immediately if such a deadlock exists. lastly, the new commissioners should also be unequivocal on european values. there is a problem there. you have already indicated the problem. mr navracsics may be competent to be a commissioner, but perhaps not with the portfolio you assigned to him. you announced a few minutes ago that he should no longer be responsible for citizenship. i think that is a step forward, but does it solve the whole problem? in writing. - on 1 july 2013, the republic of croatia joined the european union and became its 28th member state. on the same day, the additional protocol to the eu-korea fta was signed to take account of this accession and has been applied provisionally since that date. this council decision therefore seeks to ensure, in accordance with the act of accession of croatia to the european union, that that member state will continue to participate fully in the eu-korea fta, which remains in force. the approval of this council decision by the european parliament is mandatory in order to complete the process of ratification of the additional protocol and contributes to preserving the integrity of the union's internal market.
in writing. - i welcome this own-initiative report by the european parliament on the european semester, as it not only highlights the key areas that need to be reformed most urgently, but also points out the shortcomings in its implementation. the european semester is a cycle in which eu member states coordinate their economic and fiscal policies. the key to this is the country-specific recommendations, which provide concrete and tailor-made guidance for each member state's fiscal, economic and employment policies. the aim of the semester is to ensure sound public finances, to promote economic growth and to prevent excessive macroeconomic imbalances. not only is there a lack of coherence between european commitment and the implementation of the recommendations by the member states, but the involvement of national and regional parliaments and the european parliament is also low. while the eu commission's recommendations should leave political space for member states to design policies and specific reforms, they should also propose reforms that are credible. the joint action in the context of the semester is to be understood as a partnership with a clear division of competences between the eu and the member states. the early and maximum involvement of parliaments must also be ensured.
in writing. - certain aspects of the proposal emphasize the need for an ambitious initiative based on an investment plan to revive and support economic growth and above all job creation, and i can only welcome this. however, there are still some points in this report which are unacceptable. first, the mystery of where the €300 billion promised for the investment came from remains. indeed, we still do not know whether this money will come from savings on other policies or whether it is so-called 'fresh money'. this text should have emphasised more the crucial importance of public investment. especially when you consider the frugal nature of private investment. this public investment can, for example, make it possible to create industrial zones and motorways, but also to implement an energy development plan that we are so lacking. in other words, it is one of the main keys to economic recovery and to the future. social protection and workers' health also remain a sensitive issue in this report. the rights of workers are barely mentioned, especially when it is said that the red tape will be abolished through refit.

the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the council is asking for urgency to allow certain member states to spread out payments to the union budget which they should have made before 1 december under the rules they have set themselves. the urgent need today, ladies and gentlemen, is not to grant payment facilities to certain member states, even though the pill may be bitter for some. the urgent need today is to approve a union budget for 2015 that will enable the union to function properly and to honour the commitments and priorities it has set. the urgent need today is to approve the 2014 amending budgets, a necessary step to stabilise, i say stabilise and not reduce, the amount of unpaid invoices which, without this, will reach 30 billion euros by the end of this year. the urgent need today is to agree on a multiannual plan for the gradual settlement of arrears in order to avoid the union budget being suffocated in the future, either by a radical reduction in commitment appropriations, as some would like, or by unbearable delays in the settlement of invoices. the urgency requested by the council is not justified in any way. voting for urgency would be giving the council a bonus for having paid more attention to its internal balances than to the union's credibility in honouring its commitments.

president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i want to say to the members who have spoken that your concerns are our concerns. you have said it, of course, the ball is much more in the council's court and this time we want to play it much better. the fundamental point you have raised is the fight against social inequalities. it is a key point, which is why we believe that the social fund and the structural funds must increasingly be the real financial pillars of this new social dimension which we want to develop in the europe 2020 strategy. a strategy which the presidency also wants to make greener, more ecological. that's a topic you've raised. i remind you that we opened our presidency semester by bringing together, for the first time, the ministers of the environment and the ministers of labour, because we believe that green jobs are what has been missing so far in the europe 2020 strategy and we are convinced that by integrating these processes much more we will be more effective and we can achieve better results of which we can be much more satisfied than we are today in the light of what we have not been able to do.
in writing. in the context of the eu2020 strategy, we have committed to helping at least 75% of all europeans aged 20-64 to find a job by 2020, reducing the number of early school leavers to below 10% and lifting at least 20 million europeans out of poverty. we must ensure that these objectives are effectively achieved. we can do this by investing much more in our young people, by ensuring that they are able to work. this can be done, inter alia, through the youth guarantee scheme, but also by setting specific objectives for youth employment in the context of the review of the eu 2020 strategy. the investment programme to combat unemployment announced by commission president juncker can play an important role in maintaining and creating jobs. we also need to devote more resources to the fight against poverty. today, about 1 in 4 eu citizens live at risk of poverty and social exclusion. we can't just stand by and take this. we need to give people opportunities, give them a future.

in writing. - this proposal is linked to the fourth railway package which encourages more innovation and increased investment in the union's rail system. i voted in favour of this protocol because it will facilitate the offer of financing for railway rolling stock. i believe that this will not only encourage capital investment in the railway sector but also help to create a genuine market for the rental of mobile equipment in europe.
in writing. the convention, including its protocols, aims to address the problem of the establishment of secure and easily enforceable rights in respect of property which, by its nature (e.g. railway rolling stock), has no fixed location. the protocol, by offering a better international guarantee to creditors investing in the railway sector - in particular by completing the european vehicle registration number system and allowing 24-hour registration and search - will eventually create a genuine rental market for mobile equipment equipment in europe.
in writing. according to the proposal, the objective of the rail protocol is to facilitate the offer of financing for high value railway rolling stock by creating a strong international guarantee for creditors, whether credit sellers or credit providers for such sales. this should not only encourage capital investment in the railway sector but also contribute to the creation of a genuine market for the rental of mobile equipment in europe.
in writing. - the hague convention on jurisdictional arrangements of 30 june 2005 is an agreement concluded within the framework of the hague conference on private international law on exclusive jurisdictional agreements in civil or commercial matters. the convention contains provisions on the limitation of its scope, the establishment of jurisdictional arrangements, jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement and the regulation of procedural matters. the european union has already taken up this private law issue by revising the brussels i regulation. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the field of competition policy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the field of competition policy. the convention should therefore be approved.
in writing. - the convention applies in international situations to exclusive choice of court agreements concluded in civil or commercial matters. it seems to me that it is essential at the present time to have a standardisation of international contracts in order to promote trade between states. this will provide greater consistency and legal certainty for exclusive international agreements.
in writing. - this proposal for a council decision excludes from the scope of the convention insurance contracts concluded by consumers in order to prevent them from accepting a choice-of-court clause without their knowledge. the declaration annexed to the draft decision formalises this exemption and also leaves a margin of discretion for large commercial insurance and reinsurance contracts. a review declaration allows for a further analysis of this reservation in the future. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in the case of the finnish company stx finland, which is active in shipbuilding, a total of 577 workers have been made redundant. in the finnish region of rauma, the redundancies have led to an increase in the unemployment rate of over 2%. finland had justified its request for the european globalisation adjustment fund by stating that the global shipping industry had changed dramatically in recent years and that the eu's market share in this sector had decreased sharply. in particular, shipbuilders from asian countries have an advantage over european shipbuilders due to the low labour costs. the country will receive eur 1 426 800 from the fund. the fund will provide personalised services for reintegration into the labour market, including coaching, placement, training, retraining and expert services.
in writing. - the shipbuilding sector in finland is a national employment generator. unfortunately, the shipbuilding industry is facing increased competition from asian countries where labour is cheap. the resulting decline in production volume was fatal for the finnish company rauma. following this catastrophe for the local economy, great solidarity is needed with the 565 workers laid off. i therefore support the mobilisation of eur 1 426 800 from the egf to enable the former rauma workers to return to work.
in writing. i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund for finland, which was requested by the finnish authorities following the dismissal of 577 workers from stx finland oy, a shipping company, in may last year. the global shipping industry has changed dramatically in recent years: the european union's market share in shipbuilding reached only 5% in the first three quarters of 2013 compared to 13% in 2007, while the combined market share of china, south korea and japan increased from 77% in 2007 to ... 86% in the first three quarters of 2013. the considerable expansion of asia in the shipbuilding market, the decline in orders due to the economic crisis, has led to a global overcapacity in the european sector, which is causing increased competition to the detriment of workers. we have to help them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this aid. as a reminder, on 14 october 2014, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of finland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by stx finland oy in may 2014, supplemented by additional information, the latest of which was received on 22 july 2014. the commission concluded, having regard to all the relevant provisions of the egf regulation, that the application fulfilled the conditions for the granting of financial contributions from the egf. the finnish authorities argue that the global shipping industry has changed dramatically in recent years and that in this global context the european union's market share has fallen. the union market share in shipbuilding, calculated on the basis of production volume, reached 5% in the first three quarters of 2013, compared to 13% in 2007. by comparison, the combined market share of china, south korea and japan was 86% in the first three quarters of 2013, compared to 77% in 2007.
in writing. in a region where the agri-food sector is a major employer, the position of a company such as gad is of crucial importance because of the serious consequences it can have. it is therefore essential to pay particular attention to the situation of the 760 workers made redundant as a result of the increase in pigmeat prices caused by the global financial and economic crisis. therefore, the mobilisation of eur 918 000 by the egf to help reintegrate these 760 people into the labour market seems to me to be fully justified.
in writing. i welcome the decision taken by the european parliament to provide eur 918 000 of assistance to the 760 redundant employees of the french company gad through the european globalisation adjustment fund. gad, a company active in the slaughter and processing of meat, has been hit hard by the global economic and financial crisis and the decline in meat consumption. the financial difficulties of gad are thus directly linked to a major change in the structure of world trade. that is why we felt it was essential to help the workers in this company through the european globalisation adjustment fund.
in writing. i supported the vote on this report which seeks to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund in favour of the 744 workers of the french agri-food company gad who were made redundant in june 2014. the company has suffered serious difficulties, including unfair competition within the internal market from companies which have abused the directive on the posting of workers, and i repeat my request that this directive be revised as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted for this aid. as a reminder, on 24 october 2014, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of france to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by gad, a simplified public limited company active in the economic sector classified in nace rev. 2 division 10 (food industries), as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. the french authorities argue that the global financial and economic crisis has led to a decline in the consumption of pigmeat in europe, which in turn has led to a decrease in pigmeat production and in slaughterhouses such as gad. while pigmeat consumption in 2007 was still 43 kg per year per capita, it was only 39 kg per year in 2013. this decline in consumption, due to the global financial and economic crisis, affected other types of meat, but was particularly severe for pigmeat, whose price had increased faster than that of other meats, especially beef.
in writing. - on 2 december 2010, the council adopted a decision and a negotiating directive authorising the commission to open negotiations, on behalf of the eu, on an agreement with canada on the transfer and processing of passenger name records in the context of the fight against terrorism. the court of justice has ruled that the retention of personal data is not subject to the obligation to provide information to the public. the purpose of the agreement is to define the conditions under which passenger data records may be transmitted and used and how data should be protected. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the agreement is not applied to the territory of the member states. that is why i have rejected this motion for a resolution.
in writing. the council has requested the european parliament's consent to the agreement on the processing of pnr data signed with canada on 25 june 2014. on 30 september 2013, the european data protection supervisor delivered an opinion on the agreement questioning the necessity and proportionality of pnr systems and bulk transfers to third countries, as well as the choice of legal basis. on 8 april 2014, the court of justice declared the data retention directive invalid. it was therefore appropriate to refer the matter to the court of justice as to whether the draft agreement with canada is compatible with the provisions of the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights as regards the right of individuals to the protection of personal data.
in writing. - the n-va is committed to privacy and data protection. at the same time, we recognise the importance of international pnr (passenger name records) agreements for the protection of the rights and safety of eu citizens, in particular in the fight against trafficking in human beings, child exploitation, organised crime, drug trafficking, terrorism, increasing radicalisation and the current challenge of foreign fighters. we therefore want to give an explicit reason for our support for the speedy implementation of the new eu-canada pnr agreement. first, data from european citizens are currently exchanged under the old framework agreement with canada (2006) which is considerably less stringent. the new agreement includes more rights for citizens, better data retention rules and increased independent monitoring. additional advice to the court would lead to a significant delay, which would prolong the duration of the less stringent rules and reduce the protection of eu citizens. secondly, it is important that the eu works on clear european rules for data exchange with third countries with a better protection of eu citizens as a result.
in writing. in the name of the fight against terrorism, an agreement has been agreed between the european union and canada on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data. this data, which includes various information such as name, address, passport and credit card numbers, routes and travel agency, is provided by passengers and collected by airlines. however, before it can enter into force, it must first be approved by the european parliament. in voting in favour of the request for an opinion of the court of justice, we make it a precondition that the agreement be compatible with the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights and thus reiterate the importance of ensuring a balanced approach between the need to ensure the security of our citizens and their right to privacy and the protection of their data. as a liberal i am committed to finding a middle ground between these two values.
in writing. with this vote, parliament decided to refer the agreement on the transfer of european air passenger data to canada (the 'pnr' agreement) to the court of justice of the european union. doubts were raised about: 1) the legal basis of this agreement and its necessity, as the european commission had not demonstrated the need for the massive collection and storage of data; 2) proportionality (to the extent that the five-year retention period appears to be random and not based on precise evidence); the processing of pnr data is not subject to the provisions of this regulation and the processing of pnr data is not subject to the provisions of this regulation. the european parliament will therefore ask the court about the legality of mass data transfers to third countries and its compliance with european law before voting on this agreement signed last june between the european union and ottawa.
in writing. - we consider that there is legal uncertainty as to whether the draft agreement is compatible with the provisions of the treaties (article 16) and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union (articles 7 and 8 and article 52 (1)) as regards the right of individuals to the protection of personal data. i also question the choice of the legal basis, namely article 82 (1) (d) and article 87 (2) (a) of the feu treaty (police and judicial cooperation), rather than article 16 of the feu treaty (data protection); i therefore support the decision to refer the agreement to the court of justice for an opinion on its compatibility with the treaties.
in writing. - as the united nations millennium declaration of 2000, which sets the goal of significantly reducing world poverty, expires next year, a new declaration on global development goals for the period after 2015 is currently being drawn up. a systematic approach is still needed to successfully combat poverty. in this context, the european parliament urges member states in this resolution, inter alia, to honour their commitment to spend at least 0.7% of their gni, including at least 0.2% of gni for the least developed and other particularly vulnerable countries, on official development assistance. it is also necessary for the eu to present a confident and coherent position on the setting of clear targets for development aid.

in writing. we are only a few months away from the deadline for the millennium development goals (mdgs) adopted by the united nations in 2000. despite progress in the eight priority areas of action, there is still a long way to go and many challenges to be met: human rights violations, violence against women, conflict, terrorism, climate change, food insecurity, lack of access to clean water, etc. it is therefore essential to launch a thorough reflection on the post-2015 development framework. as the largest donor of official development assistance, the european union must take the lead in driving forward the adoption of an ambitious post-2015 development agenda. by voting in favour of this report, we are setting the foundations for the main directions of the european union's strategy in the ongoing negotiations for the definition of the post-2015 framework.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this resolution (541 votes in favour, 96 against and 29 abstentions) which clearly expresses the european parliament's wishes for the position to be taken by the european union in the new international negotiations on the millennium development goals to be held next year. the resolution also calls for the eu to take a more active role in the fight against poverty and inequality, and for the eu to work towards making the human rights approach and the right to development a fundamental concept. the resolution also calls on the european commission to make the elimination of inequalities in access to health and education a priority and calls on the union to support its autonomous objective of equality between women and men. finally, it called on the member states to respect their commitment to allocate at least 0.7% of their gni to official development assistance.

in writing. - the europe 2020 strategy pursues two social objectives: to ensure that 75% of the eu's working population is employed and to reduce by 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by poverty and social exclusion by 2020. but in the face of the current bleak socioeconomic record (increasing poverty, growing inequality, record unemployment), both these goals will not be achieved. so it is the credibility of the strategy that is at stake here. and the european parliament had to discuss new avenues. that is why i voted for and supported a rebalancing of the strategy between financial and economic priorities and strong social priorities in order to favour social measures. that is why i also asked for joint meetings between the epsco and ecofin councils and voted in favour of the introduction of a social protection pillar which provides for an adequate minimum income system at european level in order to strengthen social convergence in the member states. finally, i voted for the social objectives to become binding, along with the economic and budgetary policy objectives in the framework of the stability and growth pact.

the rapporteur. - madam president, after what the chairman of our committee has said, i could be more succinct, but i would like to say to the council representative, mr zanetti, that despite all the efforts he has made, i am, both as a member of parliament and as rapporteur, disappointed and frankly dissatisfied. firstly, i am disappointed because my conviction is established - and it is not just my own but that of many members - that the council has spent much more time trying to settle problems between its members, following the 'mouth-to-mouth' - excuse the expression - given by mr cameron, as regards the rebalancing of the contributions of the individual member states, than trying to agree on a common position as regards the amending budgets for 2014 and 2015. i know that it is difficult for some member states to have to spend a large sum of money all at once, but we cannot understand and are deeply disappointed that the council has taken so much time to deal with its own problems rather than with the european union's budget for 2014 and 2015. i am also disappointed and displeased, mr president, to hear - i believe it was you who said it - that in the kind of game between parliament and the council, when one party is satisfied with something, the other party must also be satisfied with something else. we're not playing a game. there is no match between parliament and the council! for the ecr group the cites convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora is now over 40 years old, but more than ever it is needed. cites as has already been said provides protection for no less than 35 000 animal and plant species. for example, if the african black rhinoceros was saved from extinction for the time being, this convention is one of the reasons. the world wildlife fund estimates the value of the illegal trade in endangered species and their products at $19 billion alone. that's the fourth largest illegal trade after drugs, counterfeiting and human trafficking. and the profits are often used to finance war and terrorism. cites regulates international trade so that it can be conducted in a sustainable way, with a view to human needs and the economy. indeed, 180 countries have already joined cites, including all 28 eu member states. today we are talking about the accession of the european union to the agreement. as the ecr group's shadow rapporteur, i can confirm that we support this accession. it promotes legal transparency on the precise role of the european union and its power. by the way, this is not a unicum. the eu has previously acceded to other international environmental conventions such as the bonn convention, the cartagena protocol and the nagoya protocol. i would like to stress that there are clearly defined responsibilities between the eu and the member states and that the eu's accession to cites does not affect the division of competences between the eu and the member states, nor the way in which a common eu position is determined. the only sensitive point is whether this dossier should have a dual legal basis (environment and trade). but this debate will not prevent us from adopting it in plenary tomorrow.

the illegal trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora is a global problem and therefore requires a global approach. the international cites convention is the most important instrument in this struggle. it is about the survival of rare species of animals and plants, but also about our security, about peace. after all, illegal trade in rare animals and plants and their derivatives is a multibillion-dollar business. the profits are often used to finance war and terrorism. my party, the nva, is a strong supporter of the european union's accession to cites and we voted in favour of it. until now, only individual member states have been members and the eu has been an observer. with accession, there is greater legal transparency on the precise role of the eu and we increase our leverage without compromising the division of competences between the eu and the member states.
in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) in force since 1975 is an international agreement which aims to regulate international trade in these species so that their survival is not endangered. the eu has had observer status since the original agreement only included states as parties. the amendment to the agreement, which entered into force in 2013, now allows the eu to become a full party to the agreement. this enables it to be adequately represented at cites meetings and to participate fully in the various activities of the convention. i therefore welcome the council's decision to allow eu accession, as the eu can now legally apply and enforce this convention. in addition, this accession also ensures that the eu can pursue its environmental policy objectives fully.
in writing. ‒ the european union had only observer status at the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). the vote will mean that the union will accede to cites and will thus be able to be represented at the meetings and participate fully in the work of the convention. it will thus have a say in all matters which concern it and affect it directly.
in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament has approved the accession of the european union to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). by signing the convention, the european union is strengthening control of international trade in these 35 000 species and protecting them better by imposing a system of marketing authorizations. all the member states have already signed. as the union is a major international player in the trade arena, it was essential that it provide support to the convention, which will allow it to participate in the work of the convention and to legally commit itself to implementing and enforcing the convention.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted by an overwhelming majority of 641 votes this afternoon to say yes to the eu's accession to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). it must be said that the current situation is extremely serious with this unprecedented wave of species extinction. some figures are unassailable: 20,000, the number of african elephants killed in 2013, 2,000 horns, the number of new rhino horns entering the trade last year, 9,500, the number of ads on the internet for wildlife trafficking, 54% of which are for live animals. there are 35,000 protected species worldwide, including the largest land mammals, and europe is the third largest destination region for illegal wildlife activity after japan and the united states. this means that it is important for the union to speak with one voice in the conference of the parties, the decision-making body of cites. the union's accession to cites is simply a welcome and logical transfer of sovereignty to protect the fragile diversity of our planet as best as possible.
in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is a crucial international instrument for the protection of endangered species of fauna and flora. the convention entered into force in 1975 and now has 178 states parties (including all the member states of the european union). cites covers more than 35 000 species and ensures that international trade in specimens of these species does not threaten their survival (all imports, exports, re-exports and introductions from the sea of species covered by the convention are subject to a system of authorization). the original text of the convention provided that membership of cites would be limited to states only. the european union has thus only had observer status until now. the proposal for a council decision which i voted for today is to approve the accession of the european union to cites. the union's accession to cites will now allow it to be adequately represented at the meetings and to participate fully in the work of the convention. i'm glad to hear it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which aims to help defend the more than 35 000 species listed in one of the three annexes to the convention and ensures that international trade in specimens of these species does not threaten their survival. all imports, exports, re-exports and introductions from the sea of species covered by the convention are subject to a system of authorization. a text that goes in the right direction.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft council decision. by virtue of the act of accession of the republic of croatia (the 28th member state to accede to the european union on 1 july 2013), croatia undertakes to become a party, under the conditions laid down in that act, to the agreement on the european economic area, in accordance with article 128 of the agreement. the republic of croatia is therefore incorporated into the eea agreement as a contracting party by the proposed agreement. i would remind you that the agreement on the european economic area (eea) was signed on 2 may 1992 and entered into force on 1 january 1994. the eea agreement ensures the free movement of goods, services, capital and people (the four freedoms) and also includes agreements on competition policy, consumer protection or education between the 28 eu member states and iceland, norway and liechtenstein.
in writing. ‒ croatia's participation at economic level is only the logical consequence of its accession, so there was no reason to vote against it. the eea agreement provides for the integration of union legislation on the four freedoms (free movement of goods, services, persons and capital) in all eea countries. the agreement also covers cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, known as 'accompanying and horizontal policies'. the agreement guarantees individuals and economic operators equal rights and obligations in the eea internal market.

in writing. france includes 5 of the 8 outermost regions of the european union (guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique, saint-martin, réunion). the eu is very concerned about the economic and social development of these regions, which suffer from the marginalization linked to their geographical specificities such as remoteness, insularity, difficult terrain and climate, dependence on a few local products, etc. they are among the priorities of the eu's cohesion policy, whose main objective is to reduce economic and social disparities across europe. it is therefore important to allow france to apply a differentiated taxation system (gratuit de mer) for certain products from these regions in order to support their competitiveness and their economic and social development. however, this system must not be contrary to the cohesion of the internal market and the legal order of the european union. it is therefore essential to establish a new regime for maritime concessions and to define its legal framework.

for the greens/efa group mr president, you are right: this parliament is the parliament of last resort here in europe. if we want to reconcile our citizens with the very idea of european integration, we must - as you have often said - bring europe closer to the citizen. but what does it mean to bring europe closer to the citizen, if not to ensure that our europe works for the majority of our fellow citizens, and not just for a minority? if we are to achieve this, i think we have to follow three lines. the first is social justice. you have told us that you want europe to deserve a triple a social status and we can only agree with you on this. some people will say: 'social policy is not a matter for the european union.' quite the contrary! first of all, let us talk about tax justice: you have already announced some initiatives on this subject which, although not going as far as they should, at least represent progress in the right direction. there is still a lot to be done in terms of tax transparency and these are relatively easy things from a political point of view to implement. we therefore encourage you to do so. we also think - and i did not hear this in your speech or in that of mr timmermans - that, contrary to what was heard this morning in plenary, the economic governance package must be revised to make the social objectives of reducing poverty and inequality and the environmental objectives as binding as the budgetary objectives. the budgetary choices that governments make will thus be choices that reduce inequalities and our ecological footprint, rather than making them worse. we must also review - and i have not heard this either - the directive on the posting of workers and stop using the six-month period to put workers on this continent, especially the most vulnerable, in competition with each other. finally, you must set up a social impact assessment of all the measures, including the budgetary measures you wish to take. the second is environmental sustainability. i keep hearing from the council, from parliament and from the commission that the ecological transition of the economy is a burden. "we'll do it when things get better", they say. yet for europeans, it is both a requirement - we continue to depend on the outside for our energy - and an opportunity! this is how we will put europe at the forefront of the next industrial revolution. the third and final axis concerns the need to remedy the democratic deficit. i've heard some ideas about transparency in lobbying. what i did not hear was that the european semester, the instrument par excellence for the convergence of policies in europe, should be subject to much deeper democratic control, both at the level of the european parliament and the national parliaments. we really need to give legitimacy to the discussions that are currently taking place when country-specific recommendations are being drawn up - recommendations that more often than not are the result of back-room agreements between government representatives, often at civil servant level, and commission representatives, without either being accountable to democratic representation. in fact, measures are taken or imposed without anyone bearing the political cost. at this point, we are no longer in a democracy. i shall end with the question of better regulation. mr timmermans, you have told us that better regulation does not mean no regulation or deregulation. you said some interesting things about the "waste" package, and i'm taking note. i would like to be assured that the air quality measures are no longer being withdrawn. finally, as regards refit, it is a device used, including by a majority of this house - i am a democrat, so i recognize it - to continually weaken the social and environmental protection measures we need if we are to lead, especially the most fragile among us, a decent life. refit cannot be the pretext for a large-scale deregulation operation. in conclusion, i would urge you to show a better sense of customer service. i was very surprised to see that it took five days - five days! - for commissioner hill to respond to the letter sent to him by the banking federations, asking for the withdrawal of the directive on structural reforms in the banking sector. it took him five days to get it back on its own! a real customer service responds instantly to this kind of demand from the big banks; the commissioner should really make a much more enthusiastic lawyer of him than he is now. we are of course opposed to the withdrawal of this directive. the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, at the beginning of the negotiations, the european parliament, through the committee on budgets, set itself three objectives. the first objective was to stabilise - if not reduce - the worrying, if not unsustainable, level of unpaid bills: 5 billion in 2010, almost 25 billion at the end of 2014. so the first priority is to stabilize the arrears. the second objective was to settle the dispute between us and the council - and the council alone, for that matter - concerning the budgetary status of the special instruments, particularly for payments. the third and most important objective was to agree with the other two institutions on the urgency of implementing a plan to reduce the amount of unpaid invoices to a sustainable level. what can we say now, after the long weeks of negotiations we have had? i would point out that the term 'negotiation' is a bit of a misnomer, since at most meetings we have had to hear the council say that it was unfortunately unable to reach a common position. as regards the balance sheet and, first of all, payment appropriations, the agreement provides for an additional fresh money of 3.529 billion for the year 2014 - and for 2014 alone - or two thirds of what we originally demanded. i would point out that we had committed ourselves to asking what the commission considered necessary namely 4.7 billion in 2014 to avoid a deterioration in the situation as regards the amount of unpaid invoices. as regards the budgetary status of the special instruments, the dispute between the council's position on the one hand and that of the european parliament and the commission on the other has not been settled. although a temporary solution, apparently neutral, was adopted for eur 350 million of unused margin appropriations, the substantive question was not settled. as regards the plan to pay off the increasing amount of unpaid invoices, which was essential for us, an agreement was reached, which i consider to be a very positive one. the commission will present an updated assessment of the overall amount of arrears and propose alternative scenarios in march 2015. the three institutions will commit themselves to implementing a plan. and i will quote this sentence, which sums up the commitment we are asking the council to solemnly formalize before us: 'this plan will be validated by the three institutions in good time before the presentation of the draft budget for 2016'. in short, overall, we think that the agreement reached between the two arms of the budgetary authority is acceptable and deserves our support, as the committee on budgets did on monday evening by a very large majority. that being said, madam president, i cannot ignore a few small mediocrity: 30 million here, 11 million there, in terms of redeployment, which the council has taken the honour of granting to one or the other of the recalcitrant member states. i do not think that mediocrity makes its authors great. i cannot forget the council's obsession with granting requests from one or another member state to extend the supplement due under the revaluation of their gni, which it had accepted. we have a text on this subject, which i am co-rapporteur with mr lewandowski; i will leave it to him to table this text, which i will vote for with no eyebrows because it is part of the agreement, whatever my thoughts on the verbal gestures of the honourable prime minister which are the cause of this misstep. i have a lot more to say, madam president, but i will save it for the last two minutes.
the rapporteur. mr president, madam commissioner, mr president of the council, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow the page will be turned, at any rate for 2014-2015, and there is no point in regretting. besides, regrets are not a policy. i think the best thing to do now is to look to the future. i think there are three things that are important for the future. as far as the immediate future is concerned, we have reached an agreement between the three institutions on the plan for the settlement of arrears within the deadlines which have been set. we will therefore ensure that this plan for the clearance of accounts becomes a reality and that all the institutions respect their commitments. in the medium term, several speakers have said so, but it is obvious: the present system is gradually coming to a standstill and will lead to a deadlock, since it is based on the contributions of the member states, drawn from their national budgets. the question of own resources is going to become a political emergency. we can feel that if we continue with the current logic, all the member states will become little margaret thatcher's, demanding their money back, and gradually this will lead to a total impasse. i am convinced that if we continue with the current logic, the support of the citizens for the european budget will not increase in the coming years. the expenditure and means of payment are mainly passed through intermediary institutions, which forget to tell the citizens that the money they receive comes from the european institutions. i am convinced that if we want to legitimize the european budget in the eyes of public opinion in the future, we must find a way - not for now, but it will be necessary - to establish a direct link, so that the european citizen perceives the effort being made in common for the benefit of all. i would like to thank the delegation from the european parliament. it was a great experience, under the leadership of our president, and i am proud to have worked with the colleagues, whom i would like to thank again.

take the decision: the 28 member states enter the guarantee scheme. that is the decision to take and you do not need to change the stability pact for that, you can do that under the rules in force today. secondly, to help the fund by saying, maybe at national level, that ok, national states should not put taxation on the income of that fund, so that not just institutional investors but also normal citizens, european citizens, can invest in the future of europe. three, you have to decide on conditionality. you have to decide with the european council tomorrow that the first investments are going to go to those countries which are carrying out positive structural reforms, as a positive incentive to carry out these reforms. the fourth point: the telecoms package. you are asking how we are going to emerge from the crisis? we have a council. decide on the telecoms package! it has been on the table of the council for months already and the only thing you are doing is going backwards: not getting rid of the roaming charges, not in fact establishing net neutrality, not in fact harmonising spectrum policy too. decide on this! this is a package that has already been more than a year on your table, so that you can create a digital market in europe. the fifth thing to decide: a second package on digital, because we need as fast as possible one regulator in the digital market. half of the countries in europe still cannot use spotify, cannot use netflix, because we do not have one regulator and we do not have one copyright regime. next thing, take the decision finally to launch the energy community. take that decision so that the commission is backed by this council to do the legislative work. and then finally: mr kamall was talking about this, it is fine that mr kamall has now discovered the advantages of a unified europe; ok we are on the right track now because he has talked about capital markets. yes indeed, we do not have one credit market, we do not have one mortgage market in europe. if you have an asset in one country you cannot use it to have credit in another country from a financial institution. so those are the decisions that you have to take. not these fake conclusions that we always see after a european council. if we see how deep this crisis is, if we see the lack of investment that we have seen since the outbreak of the crisis in 2008, what i expect from the council, not only from the italian presidency but from the 28 member states, is that now for the first time they take firm decisions to help this commission and to help us emerge from this crisis in the european union. that is your task and my request to the president of the council – i know that you are there, mr president, you are always invited at the beginning of this european council – is that you spread this key message tomorrow when you start your speech. blue-card answer. – in my proposals and in the commission proposal it is not state money that is invested in this project: it is private money that is invested in this project. so you did not even understand the commission proposal. the only thing that the european investment bank is doing, that the european budget is doing and that the member states are doing is guaranteeing a first hit if one of these investments goes in the wrong direction. that is the only thing, and that is also needed, because everybody – all the institutional investors – agree on one thing, which is that it is the cooperation between the guarantees of the state and the european investment bank on the one hand and private money on the other hand that can get us out of the crisis. so it is not public money at all! i am for private money. i am a liberal!

president, president of the council and president of the commission, i should like to begin by reading to you the title of an article in today's newspaper: "the eu wasted millions on airports". this is the result of a report by the court of auditors, which includes five airports, including one in italy, but also in greece, spain and poland. 666 million was invested in those airports and that turns out to be pretty pointless. it is about investments in airports that were not really needed, that were too close together, that are not profitable. why do i say that? firstly, because, of course, people who really have a heart for europe are always terribly embarrassed to read about it in the newspapers. i'm not saying that because i don't think we should invest. we need to invest. the socialist and democratic group is very much in favour of investment policy and wants to give it a serious boost. we also ask the council to do more, to invest more, but - and that is my message - not in any way. not in some prestige project of some minister or of some member state, but in the future. let us use criteria, criteria that have to do with sustainability and jobs, and let us prepare for the future. many have said it before, but let's do it anyway: investing in the digital agenda, human capital and the energy union. because these are investments that prepare the future, that create jobs and therefore make sense. so no prestige projects by ministers and member states that lead to nothing.
in writing. the european council must address the crucial issue of the juncker recovery plan. the lack of ambition of this plan was unfortunately confirmed a few days ago by the disappointing figures for long-term investments proposed by the ecb to encourage private investment. despite extremely favourable conditions, only 219 billion was borrowed, while the ecb wanted to reach 400 billion. this is perhaps a definitive demonstration of the need to encourage public investment in the recovery plan and job creation and thus to get out of austerity which solves nothing socially and economically. there are several important steps that can be taken in this direction. first, to finance this investment on very favourable terms. secondly, to neutralise the impact of productive public investment in the valuation of debt. but here we must go further than the immunization of investments which would pass through the european fund for strategic investments. finally, in the interests of consistency, the obstacles to such public investment, such as the strict application of the accounting standard sec2010, will have to be addressed. what is the logic of wanting to encourage public participation and, on the other hand, of imposing an accounting standard which will prevent many local and regional actors from developing their investment capacity?

in writing. for the republic of moldova, the eu introduced so-called autonomous trade preferences for the first time in 2008, eliminating all remaining customs duties on commercial goods from moldova and improving access to the eu market for agricultural products from moldova. in recent years, the eu and moldova have further intensified their political and economic relations, notably through the conclusion of an association agreement. unfortunately, in response to this enhanced cooperation, russia imposed an import ban on agricultural products from moldova, which has significantly weakened the moldovan economy. i therefore welcome all the more the fact that, as a gesture of solidarity, the eu has added three new duty-free tariff quotas for fresh apples, fresh table grapes and fresh plums to the existing tariff quotas. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to moldova, in particular through the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to moldova.
in writing. moldovan apple, grape and plum producers have suffered serious losses due to the russian embargo on moldovan agricultural products imposed by russia to put pressure on the country in the face of a rapprochement with the eu. the ban is damaging to moldova's economy, with russia as its second largest trading partner and the horticultural sector employing almost 10% of the working population. in this emergency situation, we have agreed to temporarily open liberalized access to moldovan fruit imports in order to limit the economic impact and to meet immediate needs by providing a viable market for moldovan exports. farmers are suffering the consequences of a political conflict that is beyond them. we owe ourselves compensation for the damage suffered by our neighbourhood partners. we have strengthened our political and economic ties with moldova in recent years, and it is our duty to support it financially and through targeted actions so that it is not penalized.
in writing. the agricultural sector accounts for about 40% of the moldovan economy and the horticultural sector is a significant part of it, employing some 250 000 people who live mainly in rural areas and cultivate relatively small family plots. however, following the signature of the eu-moldova association agreement on 27 june 2014, russia has banned the import of fruit from moldova. officially for... plant health reasons. under the free trade agreement with moldova, the european union has committed itself to liberalising market access for a number of fresh fruit and vegetables within certain volumes. in view of the serious difficulties that moldova is facing at the moment, i have therefore supported the proposal to temporarily increase its access to the european market for imports. the proposed preferences would bring immediate benefits and relief to the moldovan economy, while having a very limited impact on the union market.
in writing. we voted in favour of the trade agreement with moldova. i would like to point out, however, that it was strange to include a chapter on fruit when we are going through a war with russia, one of the direct consequences of which is the difficulty of getting fruit under embargo. however, it is very likely that the additional volumes of these three products entering the european market will be mostly absorbed by the romanian market, given the cultural and geographical proximity of the two countries, the similarities between their agricultural markets in terms of packaging and packaging of products, as well as the current market situation.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund was created to provide solidarity aid in the event of major natural disasters. the reason for this was the severe floods in central europe in the summer of 2002. since then, the fund has been used in many disaster situations and is thus one of the most important eu aid to the affected population within the eu's field of action. the multiannual financial framework of the eu for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund within an annual expenditure ceiling of eur 500 million. following floods in may and june 2014, serbia, croatia and bulgaria have applied for such a contribution from the fund. i therefore welcome the fact that the adoption of the decision by the european parliament will provide these countries with almost eur 80 million from the european union solidarity fund to help them deal with the consequences of the floods.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was created to provide solidarity aid in the event of major natural disasters. the reason for this was the severe floods in central europe in the summer of 2002. since then, the fund has been used in many disaster situations and is thus one of the most important eu aid to the affected population within the eu's field of action. the multiannual financial framework of the eu for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund within an annual expenditure ceiling of eur 500 million. however, in some circumstances, member states may need financial assistance in the event of a disaster more quickly than is possible under the normal procedure, which is why the possibility has been created to make an advance payment at the request of the member state concerned shortly after the commission has been asked to contribute from the fund. i therefore welcome the fact that the adoption of the decision by the european parliament will provide eur 50 million in advances and related appropriations for the financial year 2015.

in writing. the implementation of the fuel quality directive is a sensitive issue, which has been dragging on for a number of years. the 2020 deadline is getting closer and closer. so a solution is urgent. it is clear that there is no perfect solution, but the proposal put forward by the european commission and agreed with the member states is undeniably a step forward. the aim is to reduce the carbon content of road transport fuels by 6% by 2020. the commission is convinced that this objective will be achieved on the basis of the text before it. the proposal also provides for greater transparency and traceability by introducing specific reporting requirements for imports of crude oil, which is a new development. the commission proposal seems to us to be feasible, realistic and balanced. the n-va therefore voted against the objection of the environment committee and thus supported the proposal of the european commission. this does not mean that the n-va does not understand some of the concerns about the proposal, but the overall balance is rather positive.
in writing. the best is the enemy of the good: this is how one could sum up the attempt by some meps in the environment committee to change the calculation method to reduce co2 emissions in transport. the file is technical, but the answer is political: do we want to call into question the five years of work done by the european commission with the experts to put in place a calculation method as provided for in the 1998 fuel quality directive? my answer this afternoon, as well as that of 325 other members of the european parliament, is no. for at least three reasons:- it is risky to distinguish co2 emissions according to the origin of the oil used to manufacture fuels;- the calculation method proposed by the commission meets the target of reducing co2 emissions from transport by 6% by 2020. and the argument of european energy security is important. if we rejected the commission's proposal, we would have undermined the predictability of investment in the sensitive sector of the fuel industry. europe needs to ensure secure energy supply channels.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission to withdraw its proposal for a council directive and to submit a new proposal based on the requirement to report emissions according to default average values of greenhouse gas (ghg) emission intensity, broken down by types of feedstock for petrol and diesel fuel, while allowing suppliers to report actual values. the commission's text seemed to me to be too weak and unacceptable because, moreover, the proposed method for calculating the carbon intensity of the different types of road fuels did not encourage cleaner fuels and put the extremely polluting tar sands and conventional crude oil on the same footing. i also felt that the method of calculating ghg emissions from fuels and other forms of energy from non-biological sources should be further studied to take account of the expected increase in the use of fuels with high ghg emission intensity and fuels derived from other commodities in the future.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a council directive laying down the calculation methods and reporting requirements under directive 98/70/ec of the european parliament and of the council relating to the quality of petrol and diesel fuels. i am very sorry to see that this proposal has been rejected because once again some elected representatives have preferred to defend their own interests rather than the general interest.
in writing. i voted in favour of the commission delegated regulation (eu) establishing a discard plan for the baltic sea. i have also added a broader question on zero-waste and its implementation.
in writing. during the last campaign for the european elections on 25 may, the mr had pledged to make a difference in the european parliament by its action in favour of the revival of industrial sectors in difficulty, such as the steel industry. a liberal and social approach dictated by the need for results and not a purely protectionist approach which has shown its limits for more than 20 years. the reality is twofold: worrying if we consider the 60 000 jobs lost in the steel sector since 2007, promising if we consider that the steel sector represents 350 000 direct jobs and several million subcontractors in the european union. we know that the european industry is in dire need of a strong and competitive steel sector. the union is the world's second largest steel producer, accounting for 11% of total production. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment.

in writing. faced with new security challenges, europe must adapt its responses. the use of technologies and the rise of radicalisation leading to terrorism and violence require ambitious european responses in which the european union must play a leading role. it is therefore essential that it should review its internal security strategy. it must enable it to lay the foundations for its own security thinking which embraces the issues at both local and international level. it must also be a further step towards consolidating the european union's area of security and justice. however, it is imperative that the security component be fully accompanied by a counterpart based on scrupulous respect for the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which renews the european union's internal security strategy (iss) for the next four years. since the introduction of the current ssi, adopted in december 2003, new threats to security in europe and elsewhere have emerged, which now require a different political response. in fact, these security threats have become more varied, more international, more heterogeneous and more asymmetrical, requiring increased cooperation between different countries. it is also necessary to strengthen operational cooperation between member states and to this end to adopt more confidence-building measures. i am still disappointed, however, that there is no real legal dimension to the ssi. in the spirit of the stockholm programme, more should be done to strengthen mutual trust by the progressive development of a european judicial culture, to promote european cooperation and regulation in this field and to strengthen judicial cooperation in criminal matters.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. i welcome the development of a new ssi for the next four years. since the introduction of the current ssi, new security threats have emerged and others call for a different policy response. we also reaffirm that with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the charter of fundamental rights has been incorporated into union law. i sincerely believe that the current ssi needs to be fully evaluated, updated and reorganised.
