in writing. almost every day, people immigrate to the european union out of necessity. many of the asylum seekers coming to europe take the risky mediterranean route, which has become the most dangerous border crossing in the world. more than 3 000 people have lost their lives this year trying to cross the mediterranean sea to europe. the mediterranean member states are overwhelmed by this situation, which is why the european parliament, in its resolution this week, reiterated the need for a holistic approach and for the eu to assume its fair share of responsibility and solidarity towards the member states of asylum. however, in order to meet search and rescue obligations and thus prevent further deaths at sea, this also means providing adequate financial support in the medium and long term. it also calls on member states to impose strict sanctions on persons or groups exploiting vulnerable migrants in the eu and to raise awareness through wide-ranging information campaigns of the dangers to those who entrust their lives to traffickers and smugglers and to those who have been victims of trafficking.
in writing. i have of course supported this motion for a resolution by which the european parliament asks the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to examine a comprehensive eu migration strategy and to draw up a series of recommendations to strengthen it. the mediterranean has already seen too much drama. this overall strategy must therefore be based on solidarity and respect for human dignity. the eu urgently needs to develop and secure safe and legal access routes to its territory and actively combat networks of smugglers and traffickers of human beings. it must also develop greater solidarity with third countries in africa.
in writing. more than 3,000 people lost their lives in the mediterranean during the first nine months of 2014. we must find ambitious solutions so that member states can meet their international obligations and save the lives of those in danger. an ambitious approach is needed at european level to ensure effective control of migration while maintaining a humane approach. in this context, it is imperative that the eu allocates additional resources to the european agency frontex. more broadly, there is a need to consider concrete actions as soon as possible to create an effective european asylum framework and legal migration routes.
in writing. i voted for this resolution which calls for a comprehensive european approach to migration and for more efforts and financial and human resources to prevent further deaths at sea... and this despite the fact that at least 3 072 people lost their lives in the mediterranean in the first nine months of 2014! i believe that the european union should take more responsibility and show more solidarity with the member states which are hosting the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers. this necessary solidarity, which i advocate and defend, also implies making a sufficient contribution to the budgets and operations of the european border control agency, frontex, and the european asylum office.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration. it is necessary for the union to strengthen solidarity and a fair sharing of responsibilities towards the member states hosting the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers, both in absolute and relative terms, in accordance with article 80 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.

i think poland, which has admitted the existence of a secret detention facility - that they were aiding the cia's operations. the transfer of terror suspects was considered by the intelligence services of certain european member states to be too frivolous and too quick to be ok. the value of the american report is therefore primarily that it provides a mirror for our european practices. the european union says it stands for standards and values of respect for human rights for third countries. our shared european history is constantly invoked. but those principles apply to ourselves and our allies as well, and not just useful in human rights dialogue or human rights hearings. the fight against terrorism is indeed necessary and the balance between the protection of society and the infringement of personal freedoms must be right. today we see the consequences of the anti-terrorist policy that has been pursued. we see extremists in syria, iraq, afghanistan and pakistan have been able to reunite and become bloodier and more powerful by the day. the damage to europe's reputation is considerable. without prejudice to the need to combat terrorism, respect for human rights is an absolute prerequisite for ensuring the effectiveness of any counter-terrorism policy and, above all, for maintaining citizens' confidence in the democratic order of the eu. by uncritically cooperating with the cia programme, the european union has violated this trust. the unconditional use of diplomatic guarantees, the systematic invoking of state secrets and the way in which the intelligence services have assumed the role of judge are contrary to the values on which europe was built.

in writing. georgia must continue its efforts to strengthen democracy. it is important that the country continues along this path, and that is why the signing of an association agreement with it is an important and encouraging act. in addition to the benefits georgia will derive from this agreement, the european union will benefit from more regular trade flows and better investment conditions in georgia. at the same time, of course, the georgian authorities must work towards national reconciliation and continue to consolidate human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. the association agreement with georgia is a further step in strengthening the existing framework for economic and trade cooperation. it will allow us to move towards a political association based on common values and standards and towards economic integration of georgia into our internal market, through the establishment of a very ambitious free trade area, which will be beneficial to the modernisation of the country and the improvement of the quality of life of its citizens. we must continue to deepen this area of cooperation and dialogue on common interests, which will create trade prospects for the union and georgia, but also on important areas of foreign policy, security, freedom and justice. georgia has made significant progress and we must continue to show solidarity and support its reforms. the european parliament, in collaboration with the georgian parliament, has a crucial role to play in ensuring the implementation of this agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation, which is part of the approval procedure for the association agreement/free trade agreement between the european union and georgia. this agreement, which was initiated at the eastern partnership summit in vilnius on 29 november 2013 and signed on 27 june 2014, provides for enhanced cooperation in the areas of strengthening the rule of law, promoting judicial reforms, fighting corruption, ensuring respect for fundamental rights and freedoms and strengthening democratic institutions. it will also enable georgia to modernise its trade relations with the union and develop its economy through the gradual abolition of customs tariffs and quotas and the harmonisation of laws, standards and regulations. reforms are planned in the following areas: public governance, justice, law enforcement, economic recovery and growth, consumer protection, energy, transport, environmental protection, industrial and social development, social protection, education, youth and culture.
in writing. i followed the party line and my colleague who is an expert on the matter. the signing of the association agreement should mark a significant step forward in relations between the european union and georgia and embody the commitment to the method of political association and economic integration.
in writing. on 27 june 2014, georgia and the eu signed an association agreement. this agreement is part of a new generation of association agreements with eastern partnership countries and contains provisions on a deepened and comprehensive free trade area. it therefore goes beyond most free trade agreements in removing non-tariff barriers to trade, aligning regulation with the eu and including binding rules on investment and services. the eu is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy, including the establishment of a common security and defence policy. the eu-georgia association agreement is the third of its kind, following the association agreements with ukraine and the republic of moldova, for which the european parliament must give its consent to ratification. given russia's intention to significantly expand its military and economic control over the breakaway georgian territory of abkhazia, the adoption of the agreement by the european parliament is all the more welcome as it reaffirms its support for georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity and thus enables georgia to move closer to the eu in the future.
in writing. this agreement is an important step for eu-georgia relations. while the country demonstrates a real ambition to comply with the union acquis, a balanced free trade agreement will be beneficial to both parties. the eu could benefit from the facilitation of trade and the improvement of investment conditions in georgia. for its part, having adapted to european requirements in terms of laws, standards and values, georgia will not only see its political environment shifting more and more towards a democratic state based on the rule of law, but also gain access to the european market and thereby strengthen its economy.

in writing. by giving its consent to this association agreement, the european parliament will bring georgia closer to the european union. we voted in favour of the agreement and took note of the ratification of the agreement by the georgian parliament on 18 july, which paves the way for its provisional application as from 1 september 2014. it should be stressed that the association agreement will only be a success if it is implemented scrupulously by both partners. the union should therefore assist georgia in adopting the necessary laws and decrees and in ensuring their proper application.
